{"parentUuid":"e792b3b6-3fc8-49f2-b248-cc098a737284","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01GxGfEtvVmeGBaHbhFoyMB7","type":"tool_result","content":"225\t## Part 2 — See a real CMS before you design one\n226\t\n227\t**Time: 30 min. Usage cost: ~5%.**\n228\t\n229\tYou cannot be interviewed about something you have never used. Fix that first.\n230\t\n231\t### 2.1 Field trip: WordPress Playground\n232\t\n233\tOpen **`https://playground.wordpress.net`**. It runs a complete WordPress in your browser tab. Nothing installs; closing the tab wipes it. Break whatever you like.\n234\t\n235\tDo all six, in order:\n236\t\n237\t1. Write a **post**: title, a paragraph, **Save draft**. Visit the public site in another tab — it is not there.\n238\t2. **Publish** it. Reload the public site — now it is.\n239\t3. Write a **page** (\"About\"). Notice where pages show up that posts do not: the navigation menu.\n240\t4. Open **Settings → Permalinks**. Look at how the URL is built from the title. That string is the *slug*.\n241\t5. **Users → Add New**: create a user with the **Editor** role. Log out, log in as them. Try to reach **Users**. Write down exactly what happens.\n242\t6. Find where **Posts → All Posts** lets you filter by status. That screen is the content list you will build.\n243\t\n244\t### 2.2 Write your field notes\n245\t\n246\tCreate `notes/cms-field-notes.md` with **at least five** observations *in your own words*. Useful things to notice: what surprised you, what was hidden, what took more clicks than you expected, what you could not find, what an editor could not do.\n247\t\n248\tThese notes are graded (S1.1) and they are the raw material for your grill answers. Write like you are telling a friend, not like you are writing a lab report.\n249\t\n250\t### 2.3 Get the vocabulary\n251\t\n252\t```text\n253\t/clear\n254\t/research how content management systems model content, users and roles, and publishing — compare WordPress, Drupal, and static-site generators\n255\t```\n256\t\n257\tSkim the output for terms: *content type, slug, draft/published, role, capability, permalink, taxonomy, theme, headless*. You do not need all of them. You need the handful you will actually use.\n258\t\n259\t---\n260\t\n261\t## Part 3 — Your client\n262\t\n263\t**Time: 20 min.**\n264\t\n265\tYou are not building \"a CMS\". You are building one for someone, because specific people make specific demands, and those demands are what make your project yours.\n266\t\n267\t### 3.1 Pick a client\n268\t\n269\tChoose a real or plausible one you know something about: a club you belong to, a lab, a band, a campus office, a family business, a team. You will not contact them; you just need their reality.\n270\t\n271\t**If nothing comes to mind**, use the default:\n272\t\n273\t> **Knox County Historical Society.** Three volunteers run the site. Karen, the secretary, posts meeting announcements and event notices weekly; she is comfortable with email and nothing more. Tom, the president, writes longer research pieces every month or two and wants them to look permanent. Nobody should be able to edit the membership page except Tom. Their current site is a Facebook page they cannot search, and members ask them the same three questions every month: when is the next meeting, where is it, and what is on the agenda.\n274\t\n275\tIf you take the default, add **at least three details of your own** — a person, a constraint, a recurring frustration. Generic input produces a generic project, and that costs points under factor A.\n276\t\n277\t### 3.2 Write the brief\n278\t\n279\tCreate `notes/client-brief.md`. Half a page, in your words:\n280\t\n281\t- Who runs the site, and how comfortable are they with computers?\n282\t- Who reads it, and what are they usually trying to find?\n283\t- What is broken about how they do it now?\n284\t- What would make them say \"this is better\"?\n285\t- What must **not** happen? (e.g. \"a volunteer must never be able to delete the members page\")\n286\t\n287\t### 3.3 The required capabilities\n288\t\n289\tYour CMS can name things however your client would. Underneath, all seven of these must work. This list is fixed; how you get there is yours.\n290\t\n291\t1. **Login** — admins and editors sign in and out; passwords are stored hashed, never as text.\n292\t2. **Two roles** — *admin* and *editor*, with genuinely different permissions.\n293\t3. **Posts** — create, read, update, delete; title, slug, Markdown body, draft/published, author, timestamps.\n294\t4. **Pages** — same, and published pages appear in the public navigation.\n295\t5. **Admin console** — dashboard with counts, a content list you can filter, an editor with a preview.\n296\t6. **User management** — admin only: create users, change roles, deactivate; a deactivated user cannot log in.\n297\t7. **Public site and publish** — only published content, Markdown sanitized, nav built from pages, `cms publish` writes `site/` with relative paths.\n298\t\n299\t**Deliberately excluded** (do not build these): multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, rich-text WYSIWYG editors. They cost far more than they teach.\n300\t\n301\t---\n302\t"}]},"uuid":"256c14f3-62e5-4422-9ca5-a351b3605ed2","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:23:50.527Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md","content":"## Part 2 — See a real CMS before you design one\n\n**Time: 30 min. {"parentUuid":"3035e1a7-f47d-46c3-8445-9fea3a3c271a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_017SJqYuxG2ogUCk5YMTvkKx","type":"tool_result","content":"419\t## Part 6 — The loop\n420\t\n421\t**Time: 6–9 hours across several sittings. This is the project.**\n422\t\n423\t### 6.1 Grill (one session, fresh window)\n424\t\n425\t```text\n426\t/clear\n427\t/grill-with-docs I am building a small CMS for <your client, in one sentence>. Here are my field notes: notes/cms-field-notes.md and my brief: notes/client-brief.md. The 7 required capabilities are in the manual; help me decide what they mean for this client.\n428\t```\n429\t\n430\tIt asks **one question at a time**, with a recommended answer attached. How to be good at this:\n431\t\n432\t- **Answer with your client's reality**, not with generalities. \"Karen posts weekly and will never remember a slug\" is worth more than \"yes, sounds good.\"\n433\t- **Override the recommendation when you disagree**, and say why. That sentence is the single strongest evidence of your own judgment, and factor A samples exactly these answers.\n434\t- **Watch `CONTEXT.md` fill up** as terms resolve. Open it in VS Code beside the terminal.\n435\t- **Expect few or no ADRs.** They are reserved for decisions that are hard to reverse. Two are already written for you as examples.\n436\t\n437\tStop when you can answer, without hedging: what is a post here, what is a page, who may do what, what does publishing mean, and what is explicitly out of scope.\n438\t\n439\t### 6.2 Spec, then tickets (same unbroken window)\n440\t\n441\t```text\n442\t/to-spec\n443\t```\n444\t\n445\tIt turns the conversation into a spec and posts it as an issue labeled `spec`. Read the issue on GitHub. If it says something you did not decide, fix it now — everything downstream inherits it.\n446\t\n447\t```text\n448\t/to-tickets\n449\t```\n450\t\n451\t**Expected:** 7–9 issues labeled `ticket`, each with acceptance criteria and its blocking edges. Aim for tickets that look like this:\n452\t\n453\t- ✅ **T03 — Editors can create and edit posts** (touches the model, a route, a template, and tests; demoable alone)\n454\t- ❌ **T03 — Add all database models** (one layer only; nothing works until everything lands)\n455\t\n456\tThis is the **tracer bullet** idea: each ticket is a narrow but complete path through every layer, verifiable the moment it lands. If a ticket cannot be demoed by itself, split or merge it now — `/to-tickets` again with what you want changed.\n457\t\n458\tCheck your set on GitHub:\n459\t\n460\t```bash\n461\tgh issue list --label ticket\n462\t```\n463\t\n464\t### 6.3 The per-ticket runbook\n465\t\n466\tRepeat for each ticket, in blocking order. One ticket per fresh session.\n467\t\n468\t```text\n469\t/clear\n470\t/implement #3\n471\t```\n472\t\n473\tClaude reads the ticket, the spec, and `CONTEXT.md`, then drives `/tdd`: a failing test first, then code, then a green test. **You never run pytest yourself.**\n474\t\n475\tWhen it is green:\n476\t\n477\t```text\n478\t/code-review\n479\t```\n480\t\n481\tIt reviews the change in a fresh subagent against the repo's standards and the spec. Fix what it finds, or push back with a reason if you disagree — your reason is worth points under A5.\n482\t\n483\tThen, in one instruction:\n484\t\n485\t```text\n486\tPost the code-review findings and how each was resolved as a comment on issue #3, then commit and push with a message that starts \"T03:\" and ends \"Closes #3\".\n487\t```\n488\t\n489\tFinally, confirm on GitHub (10 seconds, do not skip):\n490\t\n491\t```bash\n492\tgh issue view 3\n493\t```\n494\t\n495\t**Expected:** state CLOSED, with your review comment above the closing commit.\n496\t\n497\t> **Why this order matters for your grade.** The judge checks that the ticket existed before the commit that closed it, and that a review comment arrived before the close. Those timestamps are GitHub's, not yours, which is exactly why they are trusted.\n498\t\n499\t### 6.4 When a ticket runs long\n500\t\n501\t- At **50%**, finish the current red-green cycle.\n502\t- At **60%**, at the *next green test*: `/compact keep: ticket #N acceptance criteria, what is left, files touched`.\n503\t- At **80%**, compact immediately, or `/handoff` and start fresh. Then ask whether the ticket should have been two tickets.\n504\t\n505\tIf you leave a session for a different tool, directory, or task, use `/handoff`, and copy the file it writes into `docs/handoff/{NN}_{purpose}_{YYYYMMDD}.md`. At least one handoff is required.\n506\t\n507\t### 6.5 Drift: catching the model inventing things\n508\t\n509\tDrift is when the code and your spec quietly stop agreeing: a field renamed, a rule dropped, a \"helpful\" feature nobody asked for. It is normal, and catching it is half of what this workflow is for.\n510\t\n511\tThree catches, in order of how cheap they are:\n512\t\n513\t1. **`CONTEXT.md` mismatch.** The model says \"article\" where your glossary says \"post\". Correct the vocabulary immediately; it is never only vocabulary.\n514\t2. **A test that asserts the wrong thing.** Read the test `/tdd` writes *before* you let it pass. A test written against a misunderstanding will happily go green.\n515\t3. **`/code-review` against the spec.** It compares the diff with the spec issue, which is why the spec must stay true.\n516\t\n517\tYour report has to describe **one real instance of this**: what drifted, and which of these caught it. Keep a note when it happens — you will not remember in a week.\n518\t\n519\t### 6.6 GitHub, for people who just started\n520\t\n521\t| You want to… | Command | Expected |\n522\t|---|---|---|\n523\t| See what changed | `git status` | a list of modified files |\n524\t| See your history | `git log --oneline -10` | one line per commit |\n525\t| Confirm a push landed | `gh repo view --web` | the browser shows your latest commit |\n526\t| See your tickets | `gh issue list --label ticket` | your open tickets |\n527\t| Read one ticket | `gh issue view 3` | title, body, comments, state |\n528\t| Tag a stage | `git tag mp2-mvp && git push --tags` | `* [new tag] mp2-mvp` |\n529\t\n530\t**When GitHub confuses you, in this order:**\n531\t\n532\t1. **Read the error.** Git errors usually say the fix.\n533\t2. **Ask the tool:** `gh issue --help`, `git status`.\n534\t3. **Ask Claude to explain before changing anything:** *\"I ran X and got this error: <paste>. Explain what it means and what my options are. Do not change any files yet.\"*\n535\t4. **Check the docs** linked in the troubleshooting table below.\n536\t5. **Run `/teach-log`** to record what happened and how you fixed it.\n537\t6. **Email the instructor** with the command and the full error pasted in.\n538\t\n539\t| Symptom | Cause | Fix |\n540\t|---|---|---|\n541\t| `! [rejected] … fetch first` | GitHub has commits you do not | `git pull --rebase` then push again |\n542\t| `gh: not logged in` | token expired | `gh auth login` |\n543\t| Issue did not close | commit message lacked `Closes #N` | `gh issue close 3 --comment \"closed by <sha>\"`, and use the exact phrase next time |\n544\t| `detached HEAD` | you checked out a commit or tag | `git checkout main` |\n545\t| Committed `cms.db` or `.env` | gitignore bypassed | tell Claude: *\"remove cms.db from git tracking and history, keep the local file\"* — then check `git log --all -p` |\n546\t| Push rejected: secret detected | a key reached a commit | rotate the key first, then ask Claude to rewrite history |\n547\t\n548\t---\n549\t\n550\t## Part 7 — Publish to GitHub Pages\n551\t\n552\t**Time: 30 min. Do this in Stage 1, not at the end.**\n553\t\n554\t```bash\n555\tuv run cms publish          # renders site/ from published rows\n556\tuv run cms deploy           # pushes site/ to the gh-pages branch\n557\t```\n558\t\n559\tThen, once, on GitHub: **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Deploy from a branch → `gh-pages` / root → Save**. Wait up to 10 minutes, then open `https://<username>.github.io/iphs400-mp2-cms/`.\n560\t\n561\t**Relative paths matter.** Your site lives in a subfolder, so `/style.css` (leading slash) breaks while `style.css` and `../style.css` work. In MP1 seven sites would have broken on deploy for exactly this reason. Check before you submit:\n562\t\n563\t```bash\n564\tgit grep -n 'href=\"/\\|src=\"/' gh-pages -- '*.html' | head\n565\t```\n566\t\n567\t**Expected:** no output.\n568\t\n569\t| Symptom | Fix |\n570\t|---|---|\n571\t| 404 after 10 minutes | Pages not enabled, or wrong branch selected |\n572\t| Page loads, no CSS | root-absolute paths; see above |\n573\t| Old content | you edited rows but did not re-run `cms publish` |\n574\t| Draft content is public | your publish step is not filtering on status — that is a bug, and a security-ish one |\n575\t\n576\t---\n577\t\n578\t## Part 8 — Submitting"}]},"uuid":"439d5004-2878-4a21-bfc0-765e937bcda7","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:23:51.736Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/manual_iphs400_mp2-web-cms_20260922.md","content":"## Part 6 — The loop\n\n**Time: 6–9 hours across several sittings. Keep a note when it happens — you will not remember in a week.\n\n### 6.6 GitHub, for people who just started\n\n| You want to… | Command | Expected |\n|---|---|---|\n| See what changed | `git status` | a list of modified files |\n| See your history | `git log --oneline -10` | one line per commit |\n| Confirm a push landed | `gh repo view --web` | the browser shows your latest commit |\n| See your tickets | `gh issue list --label ticket` | your open tickets |\n| Read one ticket | `gh issue view 3` | title, body, comments, state |\n| Tag a stage | `git tag mp2-mvp && git push --tags` | `* [new tag] mp2-mvp` |\n\n**When GitHub confuses you, in this order:**\n\n1. **Read the error.** Git errors usually say the fix.\n2. **Ask the tool:** `gh issue --help`, `git status`.\n3. **Ask Claude to explain before changing anything:** *\"I ran X and got this error: <paste>. {"parentUuid":"1b8b46d0-9b9a-434c-9ed0-18c2a2508e20","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01W7PcV741zq424vTbxUUkSq","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n4\t**Date:** 2026-09-22\n5\t\n6\t## Context\n7\t\n8\tA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\n9\tonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\n10\thosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\n11\tattractive target the moment it is public.\n12\t\n13\t## Decision\n14\t\n15\tThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n16\t`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\n17\tis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n18\t\n19\t## Consequences\n20\t\n21\t- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n22\t- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n23\t  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n24\t- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n25\t  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n26\t- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n27\t\n28\t## Why this is an ADR\n29\t\n30\tIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\n31\tis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\n32\tdecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n33\t"}]},"uuid":"2b5673a5-0ec7-4df1-bc11-a0f892706987","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:23:52.281Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-001-local-admin-static-public.md","content":"# ADR-001: The admin console runs locally; the public site is a static export\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nA CMS needs a server, a database, and login. GitHub Pages serves static files\nonly: it cannot run Python and has no database. Students have two weeks and no\nhosting budget, and a first web application with real authentication is an\nattractive target the moment it is public.\n\n## Decision\n\nThe admin console (FastAPI + SQLite) runs on the student's own machine. A\n`cms publish` step renders the published content to static HTML in `site/`, which\nis deployed to GitHub Pages on the `gh-pages` branch.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Login, roles, and the database are never exposed to the internet.\n- The public site cannot have server-side features (search, comments) without a\n  different host; a stretch goal may add a live admin deploy behind a security gate.\n- Publishing is explicit: content changes are not live until `cms publish` runs,\n  which is a behaviour worth documenting for your client.\n- Relative paths become mandatory, because Pages serves the site from a subfolder.\n\n## Why this is an ADR\n\nIt is hard to reverse (it shapes every route, template, and deploy step) and it\nis surprising without context (most CMSes are servers). That is the bar; most\ndecisions do not meet it and belong in the spec or the glossary instead.\n","numLines":33,"startLine":1,"totalLines":33}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1b8b46d0-9b9a-434c-9ed0-18c2a2508e20","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"15ae8495-eb67-4e64-a89e-25a063f95af9","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XrKVzqNUUEmrLwHEjhPkKZ","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n2\t\n3\t**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n4\t**Date:** 2026-09-22\n5\t\n6\t## Context\n7\t\n8\tThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\n9\tgradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\n10\tconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\n11\tread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\n12\ta build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n13\t\n14\t## Decision\n15\t\n16\tFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\n17\tand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n18\t\n19\t## Consequences\n20\t\n21\t- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n22\t  which makes debugging visible.\n23\t- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n24\t  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n25\t- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n26\t- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n27\t  here than in a JavaScript stack. That is an accepted trade.\n28\t"}]},"uuid":"2ba67233-95f5-48d5-b956-3fe5ee32ba53","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:23:52.438Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-002-stack.md","content":"# ADR-002: FastAPI + Jinja + SQLite, with no frontend framework\n\n**Status:** accepted (set by the assignment)\n**Date:** 2026-09-22\n\n## Context\n\nThe project has to be readable by someone who has never built a web application,\ngradable from a clean clone, and finishable in two weeks on a $20 plan. Options\nconsidered: Django (batteries included, but a large amount of generated code to\nread), Flask (similar to FastAPI here), a JavaScript stack (a second language and\na build step), and FastAPI with server-rendered templates.\n\n## Decision\n\nFastAPI with Jinja2 templates, SQLite for storage, argon2 for password hashing,\nand an HTML sanitizer for user Markdown. No frontend framework, no build step.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- Every page is server-rendered, so \"view source\" shows what the code produced,\n  which makes debugging visible.\n- SQLite is a single file, so a grader can seed and inspect it easily. It is\n  gitignored; `scripts/seed_demo.py` rebuilds it.\n- No build step means the file you preview is the file that ships.\n- Interactive flourishes (live preview without reload, drag-and-drop) cost more\n  here than in a JavaScript stack. Read each one relevant to the topic.\n9\t- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n10\t\n11\tIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.\n12\t\n13\t## File structure\n14\t\n15\tSingle-context repo (most repos):\n16\t\n17\t```\n18\t/\n19\t├── CONTEXT.md\n20\t├── docs/adr/\n21\t│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n22\t│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n23\t└── src/\n24\t```\n25\t\n26\tMulti-context repo (presence of `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root):\n27\t\n28\t```\n29\t/\n30\t├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n31\t├── docs/adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n32\t└── src/\n33\t    ├── ordering/\n34\t    │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n35\t    │   └── docs/adr/                  ← context-specific decisions\n36\t    └── billing/\n37\t        ├── CONTEXT.md\n38\t        └── docs/adr/\n39\t```\n40\t\n41\t## Use the glossary's vocabulary\n42\t\n43\tWhen your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Read each one relevant to the topic.\n- **`docs/adr/`**: read ADRs that touch the area you're about to work in. In multi-context repos, also check `src/<context>/docs/adr/` for context-scoped decisions.\n\nIf any of these files don't exist, **proceed silently**. Don't flag their absence; don't suggest creating them upfront. The `/domain-modeling` skill (reached via `/grill-with-docs` and `/improve-codebase-architecture`) creates them lazily when terms or decisions actually get resolved.\n\n## File structure\n\nSingle-context repo (most repos):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT.md\n├── docs/adr/\n│   ├── 0001-event-sourced-orders.md\n│   └── 0002-postgres-for-write-model.md\n└── src/\n```\n\nMulti-context repo (presence of `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the root):\n\n```\n/\n├── CONTEXT-MAP.md\n├── docs/adr/                          ← system-wide decisions\n└── src/\n    ├── ordering/\n    │   ├── CONTEXT.md\n    │   └── docs/adr/                  ← context-specific decisions\n    └── billing/\n        ├── CONTEXT.md\n        └── docs/adr/\n```\n\n## Use the glossary's vocabulary\n\nWhen your output names a domain concept (in an issue title, a refactor proposal, a hypothesis, a test name), use the term as defined in `CONTEXT.md`. Don't drift to synonyms the glossary explicitly avoids.\n\nIf the concept you need isn't in the glossary yet, that's a signal: either you're inventing language the project doesn't use (reconsider) or there's a real gap (note it for `/domain-modeling`).\n\n## Flag ADR conflicts\n\nIf your output contradicts an existing ADR, surface it explicitly rather than silently overriding:\n\n> _Contradicts ADR-0007 (event-sourced orders), but worth reopening because…_\n","numLines":52,"startLine":1,"totalLines":52}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c5231c1e-3204-417e-bb0c-97937af0d7e3","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"aea9f803-327f-4cc5-a002-c61a0511098b","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01FZSZ6RvQVsATzw3A3QmWWf","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# CONTEXT.md Format\n2\t\n3\t## Structure\n4\t\n5\t```md\n6\t# {Context Name}\n7\t\n8\t{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n9\t\n10\t## Language\n11\t\n12\t**Order**:\n13\t{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n14\t_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n15\t\n16\t**Invoice**:\n17\tA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n18\t_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n19\t\n20\t**Customer**:\n21\tA person or organization that places orders.\n22\t_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n23\t```\n24\t\n25\t## Rules\n26\t\n27\t- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n28\t- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n29\t- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n30\t- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n31\t\n32\t## Single vs multi-context repos\n33\t\n34\t**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n35\t\n36\t**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n37\t\n38\t```md\n39\t# Context Map\n40\t\n41\t## Contexts\n42\t\n43\t- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n44\t- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n45\t- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n46\t\n47\t## Relationships\n48\t\n49\t- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n50\t- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n51\t- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n52\t```\n53\t\n54\tThe skill infers which structure applies:\n55\t\n56\t- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n57\t- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n58\t- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n59\t\n60\tWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n61\t"}]},"uuid":"76306e55-34f9-420e-917d-3bba0b2cb929","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:23:57.633Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/domain-modeling/CONTEXT-FORMAT.md","content":"# CONTEXT.md Format\n\n## Structure\n\n```md\n# {Context Name}\n\n{One or two sentence description of what this context is and why it exists.}\n\n## Language\n\n**Order**:\n{A one or two sentence description of the term}\n_Avoid_: Purchase, transaction\n\n**Invoice**:\nA request for payment sent to a customer after delivery.\n_Avoid_: Bill, payment request\n\n**Customer**:\nA person or organization that places orders.\n_Avoid_: Client, buyer, account\n```\n\n## Rules\n\n- **Be opinionated.** When multiple words exist for the same concept, pick the best one and list the others under `_Avoid_`.\n- **Keep definitions tight.** One or two sentences max. Define what it IS, not what it does.\n- **Only include terms specific to this project's context.** General programming concepts (timeouts, error types, utility patterns) don't belong even if the project uses them extensively. Before adding a term, ask: is this a concept unique to this context, or a general programming concept? Only the former belongs.\n- **Group terms under subheadings** when natural clusters emerge. If all terms belong to a single cohesive area, a flat list is fine.\n\n## Single vs multi-context repos\n\n**Single context (most repos):** One `CONTEXT.md` at the repo root.\n\n**Multiple contexts:** A `CONTEXT-MAP.md` at the repo root lists the contexts, where they live, and how they relate to each other:\n\n```md\n# Context Map\n\n## Contexts\n\n- [Ordering](./src/ordering/CONTEXT.md): receives and tracks customer orders\n- [Billing](./src/billing/CONTEXT.md): generates invoices and processes payments\n- [Fulfillment](./src/fulfillment/CONTEXT.md): manages warehouse picking and shipping\n\n## Relationships\n\n- **Ordering → Fulfillment**: Ordering emits `OrderPlaced` events; Fulfillment consumes them to start picking\n- **Fulfillment → Billing**: Fulfillment emits `ShipmentDispatched` events; Billing consumes them to generate invoices\n- **Ordering ↔ Billing**: Shared types for `CustomerId` and `Money`\n```\n\nThe skill infers which structure applies:\n\n- If `CONTEXT-MAP.md` exists, read it to find contexts\n- If only a root `CONTEXT.md` exists, single context\n- If neither exists, create a root `CONTEXT.md` lazily when the first term is resolved\n\nWhen multiple contexts exist, infer which one the current topic relates to. If unclear, ask.\n","numLines":61,"startLine":1,"totalLines":61}},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"aea9f803-327f-4cc5-a002-c61a0511098b","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"057c40a4-b01d-4025-9c37-774b9b815fc8","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"2603e1fb-7f78-4f15-8b1d-b91d8432dda5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_016QFz1CxHMVG1FkauYe2HuF","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"The FastAPI application.\n\nT00 (already done): the admin console answers at /admin and the public site\nanswers at /. That is the whole skeleton — it exists so you can prove the stack\nruns before you build anything on it.\n\nAdd your routes in their own modules (app/routes/posts.py and so on) and include\nthem here. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n=== SECURITY\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\n=== conftest\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n=== seed\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n=== rubric grep\n4:**Project:** Mini-Project #2 — a WordPress-style Web CMS with an admin console, built with the mattpocock/skills workflow `/grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review`\n17:## Part I — The Rubric\n19:### 1. Keep this file small.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom fastapi import FastAPI, Request\nfrom fastapi.templating import Jinja2Templates\n\nfrom app import settings\n\ntemplates = Jinja2Templates(directory=str(settings.TEMPLATES))\n\n\ndef create_app() -> FastAPI:\n    app = FastAPI(title=\"IPHS 400 MP2 CMS\")\n\n    @app.get(\"/admin\")\n    def admin_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"admin/hello.html\", {\"title\": \"Admin\"}\n        )\n\n    @app.get(\"/\")\n    def public_home(request: Request):\n        return templates.TemplateResponse(\n            request, \"public/home.html\",\n            {\"title\": settings.SITE_TITLE, \"items\": []},\n        )\n\n    # Your ticket work plugs in here, e.g.\n    #   from app.routes import posts\n    #   app.include_router(posts.router)\n    return app\n\n\napp = create_app()\n\"\"\"Render the public site into site/ as plain HTML.\n\nT00 publishes a placeholder home page. As you build content types, extend\nrender_site() to write one file per published item. Two rules the rubric checks:\n\n  1. Only PUBLISHED content is written here. A draft that reaches site/ is a bug.\n  2. Every href and src is RELATIVE (\"style.css\", \"posts/x.html\"), never\n     root-absolute (\"/style.css\"), because Pages serves this from a subfolder.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport shutil\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom jinja2 import Environment, FileSystemLoader, select_autoescape\n\nfrom app import settings\n\nCSS = \"\"\"/* Minimal starter styles — make them yours. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\nheader a { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n\"\"\"\n\n\ndef environment() -> Environment:\n    return Environment(\n        loader=FileSystemLoader(str(settings.TEMPLATES)),\n        autoescape=select_autoescape([\"html\"]),\n    )\n\n\ndef render_site(out: Path | None = None) -> Path:\n    out = out or settings.SITE\n    if out.exists():\n        shutil.rmtree(out)\n    out.mkdir(parents=True)\n    env = environment()\n    (out / \"style.css\").write_text(CSS)\n    (out / \"index.html\").write_text(\n        env.get_template(\"public/home.html\").render(\n            title=settings.SITE_TITLE, items=[], css_path=\"style.css\",\n            home_path=\"index.html\",\n        )\n    )\n    return out\n\"\"\"The `cms` command: serve, publish, deploy.\n\n    uv run cms serve      # admin console + public preview at http://localhost:8000\n    uv run cms publish    # render site/ from published content\n    uv run cms deploy     # push site/ to the gh-pages branch (Pages serves it)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\n\nfrom app import settings\nfrom app.publish import render_site\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog=\"cms\")\n    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest=\"command\", required=True)\n    serve = sub.add_parser(\"serve\", help=\"run the admin console locally\")\n    serve.add_argument(\"--port\", type=int, default=8000)\n    serve.add_argument(\"--reload\", action=\"store_true\", default=True)\n    sub.add_parser(\"publish\", help=\"render site/ from published content\")\n    deploy = sub.add_parser(\"deploy\", help=\"push site/ to gh-pages\")\n    deploy.add_argument(\"--message\", default=\"Publish site\")\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if args.command == \"serve\":\n        import uvicorn\n\n        uvicorn.run(\"app.main:app\", port=args.port, reload=args.reload)\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"publish\":\n        out = render_site()\n        print(f\"Wrote {out}. Preview it with:  python3 -m http.server -d {out} 8001\")\n        return 0\n\n    if args.command == \"deploy\":\n        if not settings.SITE.exists():\n            print(\"site/ does not exist yet — run `uv run cms publish` first.\")\n            return 1\n        result = subprocess.run(\n            [sys.executable, \"-m\", \"ghp_import\", \"-n\", \"-p\", \"-m\", args.message,\n             str(settings.SITE)],\n        )\n        if result.returncode == 0:\n            print(\"Pushed to gh-pages. Settings -> Pages -> Deploy from a branch -> \"\n                  \"gh-pages / root, then wait up to 10 minutes.\")\n        return result.returncode\n    return 1\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n=== SECURITY\n# Security checklist\n\nWhat must be true before you submit. *How* to make each one true is your work —\nthat is the point of the tickets.\n\n| # | Must be true | How the grader checks it |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Stored passwords are argon2 hashes | Reads the seeded database and looks at the stored value |\n| 2 | Wrong passwords are refused, and the message does not reveal whether the account exists | Tries a bad password |\n| 3 | Every state-changing form (POST) carries a CSRF token and rejects a request without one | Replays each POST with the token removed |\n| 4 | An editor cannot reach any admin-only route | Logs in as the seeded editor and requests each admin route |\n| 5 | An anonymous visitor is redirected to login, never shown admin content | Requests admin routes with no session |\n| 6 | A deactivated user cannot log in | Deactivates the seeded editor, then tries to log in |\n| 7 | User-written Markdown cannot inject scripts | Saves a post containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute, publishes, and checks both the preview and the export |\n| 8 | Drafts never appear in `site/` or on the public site | Publishes with a draft present and searches the output |\n| 9 | No secrets, databases, or `.env` files in git history | Greps the full history |\n| 10 | Access control is enforced in code, not by hiding links | Requests admin URLs directly rather than clicking |\n\nRule of thumb: if the only thing stopping an editor from reaching a page is that\nthe link is hidden, it is not stopping anyone.\n=== conftest\n\"\"\"Shared test fixtures.\n\n`client` gives you the app. `client_as(role)` gives you a client that is logged\nin as a seeded user of that role — it works as soon as your login route exists,\nso access-control tests stay one line:\n\n    def test_editor_cannot_manage_users(client_as):\n        assert client_as(\"editor\").get(\"/admin/users\").status_code in (302, 403)\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport pytest\nfrom fastapi.testclient import TestClient\n\nfrom app.main import create_app\n\n# Matches scripts/seed_demo.py. Passwords come from the environment there; in\n# tests they are fixed and meaningless.\nDEMO_USERS = {\n    \"admin\": {\"email\": \"admin@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-admin-pw\"},\n    \"editor\": {\"email\": \"editor@example.test\", \"password\": \"test-editor-pw\"},\n}\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client() -> TestClient:\n    return TestClient(create_app())\n\n\n@pytest.fixture\ndef client_as():\n    \"\"\"Return a factory: client_as(\"editor\") -> a logged-in TestClient.\"\"\"\n\n    def _login(role: str) -> TestClient:\n        user = DEMO_USERS[role]\n        c = TestClient(create_app())\n        response = c.post(\"/login\", data={\"email\": user[\"email\"],\n                                          \"password\": user[\"password\"]},\n                          follow_redirects=False)\n        if response.status_code == 404:\n            pytest.skip(\"No /login route yet — build the login ticket first.\")\n        assert response.status_code in (200, 302, 303), (\n            f\"Login as {role} failed with {response.status_code}\")\n        return c\n\n    return _login\n=== seed\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Create demo data so a grader (and you) can use the CMS immediately.\n\n    uv run python scripts/seed_demo.py\n\nT00 has nothing to seed. As you build content types, extend this so it creates:\n  - one admin and one editor (passwords read from .env, never hard-coded)\n  - a few posts and pages, at least one draft and one published\n\nThe rubric expects this to run clean on a fresh clone with .env.example values\n(item E4), because the database itself is never committed.\n\"\"\"\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport sys\n\n\ndef main() -> int:\n    admin_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD\")\n    editor_pw = os.environ.get(\"CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD\")\n    if not admin_pw or not editor_pw:\n        print(\"Set CMS_ADMIN_PASSWORD and CMS_EDITOR_PASSWORD in .env \"\n              \"(copy .env.example).\")\n        return 1\n\n    # TODO (your tickets): create the users, then the demo content.\n    print(\"Nothing to seed yet: no content types exist. \"\n          \"Extend scripts/seed_demo.py as you build T01+.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n=== rubric grep\n4:**Project:** Mini-Project #2 — a WordPress-style Web CMS with an admin console, built with the mattpocock/skills workflow `/grill-with-docs → /to-spec → /to-tickets → /implement → /code-review`\n17:## Part I — The Rubric\n19:### 1. {"parentUuid":"f59fed7d-764b-4da7-bf1a-cad35dff22e3","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbbC9YjDwJFbkr186VCk","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I've read your field notes, brief, the manual's seven capabilities, both ADRs, the rubric, and the template code; `CONTEXT.md` is still empty, so nothing conflicts with a glossary yet. Here is round 1.\n\nThis version of the skill asks in rounds rather than one question at a time. Answer by number, in any order, and override my recommendation wherever AWM's reality says otherwise.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q1 - One account per person, or one per position?** Your brief says \"passwords are passed down from spring semester to fall semester each year.\" That can mean two different things:\n\n- **(a) Per position:** there is one \"Treasurer\" login, and the password is handed to whoever holds the job next.\n- **(b) Per person:** every officer has their own login; each year the co-VPs create accounts for new officers and deactivate the outgoing ones.\n\nScenario: last year's Social Chair graduates in May. In September, can they still log in?\n\n➡️ **(b), per person.** Under (a) the old Social Chair still knows the password, and capability 6 (\"a deactivated user cannot log in\") has nothing to deactivate. The only thing passed down would be the co-VP handover: outgoing co-VPs create the incoming co-VPs' accounts before they leave.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q2 - What is the weekly thing called, and is it the only kind?** The manual calls it a \"post\", and your brief says \"post the Monday Study Hall info\" and \"a link to the website post.\" Two things to settle:\n\n1. Is **Post** the word officers would use, or would they say \"announcement\", \"update\", or something else?\n2. Is the weekly Study Hall post the *only* kind, or do other things get posted (a cancelled Study Hall, a finals-week change, a social event from the Social Chair)?\n\n➡️ **One content type, called Post**, meaning any dated news item. The weekly Study Hall post is the most common one, not a special type. Avoid \"announcement\" and \"update\" so we don't end up with two designs.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q3 - Where does the standing time and place live?** Your brief's pain point is \"the time and place is in 3 files.\" Hayes 311, Mondays 8–10pm has to live in exactly one place:\n\n- **(a)** A **Study Hall page** holds it; weekly posts only say what is different this week.\n- **(b)** Site-wide settings fields (day, time, room) shown in the header of every page.\n- **(c)** Retyped in every weekly post.\n\nScenario: Study Hall moves to another room for one week only, versus moving permanently.\n\n➡️ **(a).** The page is the single source and a permanent move is one edit. A one-week change is a post, and the page stays untouched. (b) is a new feature outside the seven capabilities, with Stage 2 due Tuesday Oct 6. (c) recreates the problem you have now.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q4 - Whose computer is the CMS on, and what does \"publish\" mean?** The assignment fixes that the admin console runs on a laptop, never on the internet (ADR-001). The database is not in git, so content does not travel between machines. So \"publish\" is really two steps, close to your field note 2:\n\n1. An officer marks a post **Published** in the console. It is still only on that laptop.\n2. Someone runs `cms publish` and `cms deploy` in a terminal. Now members can see it.\n\nWhere does that one copy live, and who does step 2? And what would officers call each step?\n\n➡️ **One copy on a co-VP's laptop**, with the co-VPs responsible for step 2. Use two words: **Published** for the status an officer sets, and **Go live** for pushing the site to the public. This clashes with \"a new officer can post without learning HTML\" if step 2 needs a terminal, so I will ask next round whether the console needs a button for it.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q5 - Which pages exist, and who creates them?** The brief says the site tells people when and where Study Hall is, how to join, and links to the snack request form. It also says editors edit pages but never delete them. It doesn't say who *creates* them.\n\n➡️ **Three pages: Study Hall, Join, Snacks** (the last one is mostly the Google Form link). **Only co-VPs create and delete pages**; editors edit the text of existing ones. {"parentUuid":"1ca8acfc-0369-49d3-b3e2-243d406a101e","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbcVkUGN4to5WupbaUqh","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01H3MSfcUec9Ezzc2gyntW3o","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. It belongs to the Position, not to a person.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login\n\n**Role**:\nWhat an Account is allowed to do. There are two: Admin and Editor.\n\n**Admin**:\nThe Role of the Co-VPs, who maintain the site, create and delete Pages, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n\n**Editor**:\nThe Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's.\n\n**Visitor**:\nA member or curious student reading the public site. A Visitor never logs in.\n\n### Content\n\n**Study Hall**:\nAWM's weekly meeting.\n_Avoid_: meeting\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item on the site. It is the only kind of dated content.\n_Avoid_: announcement, update\n\n**Study Hall reminder**:\nThe weekly Monday Post about that night's Study Hall. Nearly every Post is one.\n\n**Page**:\nA permanent part of the site's structure. There are three: Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n\n### Publishing\n\n**Draft**:\nA Post or Page still being written, which Visitors cannot see.\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Officer gives a Post or Page when it is ready for Visitors. Published content reaches Visitors only at the next Go live.\n\n**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5330,"cache_read_input_tokens":73653,"output_tokens":6490,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":5708},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5330,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":6490,"cache_read_input_tokens":73653,"cache_creation_input_tokens":5330,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":5330},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01H3MSfcUec9Ezzc2gyntW3o":{"file_path":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"d60e2c81-6bdb-43b0-89ca-3eb078280485","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:42:16.902Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"update","filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","content":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. It belongs to the Position, not to a person.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login\n\n**Role**:\nWhat an Account is allowed to do. There are two: Admin and Editor.\n\n**Admin**:\nThe Role of the Co-VPs, who maintain the site, create and delete Pages, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n\n**Editor**:\nThe Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's.\n\n**Visitor**:\nA member or curious student reading the public site. A Visitor never logs in.\n\n### Content\n\n**Study Hall**:\nAWM's weekly meeting.\n_Avoid_: meeting\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item on the site. It is the only kind of dated content.\n_Avoid_: announcement, update\n\n**Study Hall reminder**:\nThe weekly Monday Post about that night's Study Hall. Nearly every Post is one.\n\n**Page**:\nA permanent part of the site's structure. There are three: Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n\n### Publishing\n\n**Draft**:\nA Post or Page still being written, which Visitors cannot see.\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Officer gives a Post or Page when it is ready for Visitors. Published content reaches Visitors only at the next Go live.\n\n**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":1,"oldLines":3,"newStart":1,"newLines":62,"lines":["-# CONTEXT.md glossary","+# AWM at Kenyon CMS"," ","-(Your /grill-with-docs session fills this in as terms are settled.)","+The website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when","+and where Study Hall is and how to join.","+","+## Language","+","+### People","+","+**Officer**:","+A student who currently holds a Position in AWM.","+","+**Position**:","+A named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.","+_Avoid_: title, job","+","+**Account**:","+The login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. {"parentUuid":"af0d8fa1-bdd0-410b-88f1-3e39b31e90ef","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbcazcD96NP86eq11foq","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Round 1 is settled and `CONTEXT.md` now has 15 terms from your answers. Two of them are words I chose, so veto them if they're wrong:\n\n- **Account** for a position's login (instead of \"user\"), since you decided the login belongs to the position, not a person.\n- **Study Hall reminder** for the weekly Monday post, taken from your Q2 answer.\n\nOne thing to reconcile: in Q3 you picked a Study Hall page, but your three pages in Q5 don't include one. I read that as the Home page being the single place the time and room live. Q9 confirms it.\n\nHere is round 2.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q6 - How many accounts are there?** You have two Co-VPs and two Co-Presidents. Is that:\n\n- **(a) Four accounts**, one per position: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer. Both Co-VPs use the same login.\n- **(b) Six accounts**: each Co-VP and each Co-President gets their own.\n\nScenario: there is only one Admin account and someone deactivates it or switches it to Editor. Nobody can manage accounts any more.\n\n➡️ **(a), four accounts**, which fits your \"it isn't that top secret\" answer. Add one rule: the last active Admin account can never be deactivated or changed to Editor.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q7 - What happens to a password at Handover, and when one is forgotten?** Scenario: the new Treasurer forgets the password in October. Who fixes it, and how?\n\n➡️ **Co-VPs can set a new password for any account from the Accounts screen.** At Handover the old password can simply be passed on, or a Co-VP can change it. No \"forgot my password\" email, because the console is on one laptop and cannot send mail.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q8 - Whose name is on a post?** Capability 3 requires an author. With per-position accounts the author is a position, not a person. Your example email is signed \"- AWM <3\".\n\n➡️ **The console shows the position** (\"Social Chair\") in the content list, so Co-VPs can see who posted what. **The public site shows only the date**, with no author line, so posts read as coming from AWM like the email does.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q9 - What exactly is the Home page?** I understand it as: the standing Study Hall info (Mondays 8–10pm, Hayes 311) as editable text, with the latest post shown underneath. Three things to decide:\n\n1. Can anyone delete or unpublish Home?\n2. Does it show only the latest post, or a few?\n3. Where do older posts go, and does each post get its own link for the weekly email?\n\n➡️ **Home always exists**: nobody, including a Co-VP, can delete it or set it back to Draft, and Editors can edit its text. **It shows the single latest published post in full.** **Each post has its own link** for the email, and older posts sit on an automatic \"Past posts\" list linked from Home. That list is not a Page and nobody creates it.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q10 - What does deleting a post mean?** Your brief says Editors publish and delete posts. Scenario: Monday at 7pm the Treasurer deletes the Social Chair's Study Hall reminder by mistake.\n\n- May an Editor delete any post, or only ones from their own account?\n- Is it gone for good, or recoverable?\n\n➡️ **Any Editor can delete any post, after a \"Are you sure?\" confirmation, and it is permanent.** A trash bin is extra work with the deadline on Tuesday, and a reminder is a few lines to retype. The post leaves the public site at the next Go live.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q11 - Can an Editor change a page's status?** Setting a Published page back to Draft removes it from the navigation, which for Visitors is the same as deleting it. Your brief says an Editor must never delete a page.\n\n➡️ **No. Only Co-VPs change a page's status.** Editors change the text only. An Editor's text change to a Published page reaches Visitors at the next Go live, with no approval step.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q12 - Is Go live a button or a terminal command?** Co-VPs change every year and your brief says each new person has a different level of computing expertise. Right now Go live means typing two commands in a terminal.\n\n➡️ **A \"Go live\" button on the dashboard, Co-VP only.** It runs the same two steps as the commands. Editors don't get it, since you said Co-VPs are responsible for step 2 and it is their laptop.\n\n---\n\nOne offer: your Q1 decision (accounts belong to positions, passwords passed down) meets the bar for an ADR. It is hard to reverse, surprising to a later reader, and you chose it over per-person accounts for a stated reason. Say yes and I'll write `ADR-003` with your reasoning.\n\nStill parked: slugs for near-identical weekly titles, what the dashboard counts, and the out-of-scope list."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6575,"cache_read_input_tokens":78983,"output_tokens":1605,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6575,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1605,"cache_read_input_tokens":78983,"cache_creation_input_tokens":6575,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":6575},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"0714061e-17cb-492f-b22b-ba79eab65b1b","apiBlockIndex":0,"requestId":"req_011CfbcaycvsUKPZBD4gjKCc","type":"assistant","uuid":"5fe8a086-14ed-4724-bf60-691535e08786","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:42:33.958Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

It belongs to the Position, not to a person, so the two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share another.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login","originalFile":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. It belongs to the Position, not to a person.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login\n\n**Role**:\nWhat an Account is allowed to do. There are two: Admin and Editor.\n\n**Admin**:\nThe Role of the Co-VPs, who maintain the site, create and delete Pages, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n\n**Editor**:\nThe Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's.\n\n**Visitor**:\nA member or curious student reading the public site. A Visitor never logs in.\n\n### Content\n\n**Study Hall**:\nAWM's weekly meeting.\n_Avoid_: meeting\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item on the site. It is the only kind of dated content.\n_Avoid_: announcement, update\n\n**Study Hall reminder**:\nThe weekly Monday Post about that night's Study Hall. Nearly every Post is one.\n\n**Page**:\nA permanent part of the site's structure. There are three: Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n\n### Publishing\n\n**Draft**:\nA Post or Page still being written, which Visitors cannot see.\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Officer gives a Post or Page when it is ready for Visitors. Published content reaches Visitors only at the next Go live.\n\n**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":15,"oldLines":7,"newStart":15,"newLines":7,"lines":[" _Avoid_: title, job"," "," **Account**:","-The login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. {"parentUuid":"bf9bc3b6-7863-48ea-9397-46a77133aa10","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfbd5As8SThUnFUuowy3z","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Round 2 is settled. `CONTEXT.md` now also defines **Author**, **Weekly email** (your note that it matches the post plus a link), **Home**, and **Past posts**, and the Account entry says the two Co-VPs share one account.\n\nHere is round 3, which I expect to be the last full round.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q13 - What does an account sign in with?** The template's test helper signs in with an email address and a password, and the seeded demo accounts are `admin@example.test` and `editor@example.test`. I can't see the grader's walkthrough script, but it most likely does the same. Does AWM have an email address per position, one club address, or neither?\n\n➡️ **Keep an email-shaped sign-in**, one address per account (for example a `treasurer@...` style address, real or not). The console never sends mail, so the address is only a login name. Each account also has a display name that is the position (\"Treasurer\"), and that is what shows as Author.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q14 - What is the link to a weekly post?** The link (the slug) is built from the title, and it is what goes in the Weekly email. Nearly every post is titled something like \"Study Hall tonight!\", so titles will collide. A new officer will also never have heard of a slug.\n\n➡️ **The link is made automatically from the date plus the title** (for example `2026-10-05-study-hall-tonight`), and officers never type it. **It stops changing once the post is Published**, so a link already sent in an email never breaks, even if someone fixes a typo in the title. The Monday order becomes: write the post, mark it Published, a Co-VP presses Go live, then send the email with the link.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q15 - How does a Visitor know which Monday a post means?** Your example says \"We are CURRENTLY having our study hall tonight.\" Scenario: a curious student opens Home on Thursday and reads \"tonight\".\n\n➡️ **Every post shows its date with the weekday** (\"Monday, October 5\") right above the text, on Home and on its own page. That date is when the post was first Published. Nothing expires or hides automatically.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q16 - What does the dashboard tell an officer?** Capability 5 needs counts and a list you can filter. Scenario: the Social Chair marks the reminder Published at 6pm and leaves. Nobody presses Go live, so the email link leads nowhere.\n\n➡️ **Counts of Draft posts, Published posts, and Pages**, with the number of Accounts shown to Co-VPs only. Add **\"Last Go live: date and time\"** and a plain warning when something has changed since then (\"2 changes are not live yet\"). The content list filters by Draft/Published and by Post/Page, newest first.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q17 - What is deactivating an account for?** With one account per position, nobody \"leaves\". Two scenarios: AWM has no Social Chair for a year, or AWM adds a new position such as an outreach chair.\n\n➡️ **Co-VPs deactivate an account when its position is vacant and create one when a position is added**, choosing its Role. A deactivated account cannot sign in, but **its posts stay on the site** and can be reactivated later. Accounts are never deleted.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q18 - What is explicitly out of scope?** My proposed list of things this CMS will not do:\n\n- Send the Weekly email (it stays manual, per your brief)\n- Host the snack request form (Join & Snacks only links to the Google Form)\n- Scheduled posts or a calendar\n- Comments, or any Visitor login\n- Image uploads (this means no uploaded officer photos on About)\n- Categories, tags, or search\n- A trash bin or undo for deleted posts\n- \"Forgot my password\" emails\n- A \"copy last week's reminder\" button\n\n➡️ **All nine are out.** The last one would be useful for AWM, since 99% of posts are the same reminder, so I'd name it as the first future improvement in your report rather than build it before Tuesday. Tell me if officers would expect any of these, especially photos on About.\n\n---\n\n❓ **Q19 - Record the shared-accounts decision as an ADR?** This is the offer from last round.\n\n➡️ **Yes.** `ADR-003` would say accounts belong to positions and passwords are passed down at Handover, chosen over per-person accounts because, in your words, it isn't that top secret and former officers will hardly think about it."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"end_turn","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4877,"cache_read_input_tokens":87298,"output_tokens":1963,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":528},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4877,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":1963,"cache_read_input_tokens":87298,"cache_creation_input_tokens":4877,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":4877},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"serverClassifierRequest":"7b545888-272c-41a6-81cd-7499fc55da41","apiBlockIndex":1,"requestId":"req_011Cfbd5AR6xsTXurCEnYJcb","type":"assistant","uuid":"a2d2f608-6251-40e2-bc5b-2e6bbbdee7fc","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:49:00.453Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"84de2fcb-7e71-4552-af21-34dc88209564","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbdRzC2Cb42zSwTFT6pB","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01CejL5Ade7oMiiCh79ZRQVG","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-accounts-belong-to-positions.md","content":"# ADR-003: Accounts belong to Positions, not to people\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-01\n\n## Context\n\nAWM's Officers change every year. The client brief says \"there will be passwords\nthat are passed down from spring semester to fall semester each year.\" That can\nbe built two ways: one Account per Position, whose password is handed to\nwhoever holds the Position next, or one Account per person, created and\ndeactivated by the Co-VPs each year.\n\nPer-person Accounts are the usual choice, because a former Officer who still\nknows a shared password can still sign in. Per-Position Accounts were chosen\nanyway, for the client's stated reason: \"it isnt that top secret, former\nposition members will hardly think about it.\"\n\n## Decision\n\nThere is one Account per Position: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, and\nTreasurer. The two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share\nanother. Passwords are passed down at Handover. The Co-VP Account is the Admin;\nthe other three are Editors.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The Author of a Post is a Position (\"Social Chair\"), never a named person. The\n  console cannot tell which of the two Co-VPs did something.\n- A former Officer who remembers a password can still sign in until a Co-VP\n  sets a new one. The console runs only on a Co-VP's laptop (ADR-001), so they\n  would also need that laptop.\n- Co-VPs can set a new password for any Account. There is no \"forgot my\n  password\" email.\n- Deactivating is for a Position that is vacant, not for a person who has left.\n  A deactivated Account's Posts stay on the site, and Accounts are never deleted.\n- The last active Admin Account can never be deactivated or changed to Editor,\n  because with one shared Admin Account that would lock everyone out.\n- Moving to per-person Accounts later would mean re-deciding who the Author of\n  every existing Post is.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":56,"cache_read_input_tokens":94138,"output_tokens":2391,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":898},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":56,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2391,"cache_read_input_tokens":94138,"cache_creation_input_tokens":56,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":56},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01CejL5Ade7oMiiCh79ZRQVG":{"file_path":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-accounts-belong-to-positions.md","content":"# ADR-003: Accounts belong to Positions, not to people\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-01\n\n## Context\n\nAWM's Officers change every year. Per-Position Accounts were chosen\nanyway, for the client's stated reason: \"it isnt that top secret, former\nposition members will hardly think about it.\"\n\n## Decision\n\nThere is one Account per Position: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, and\nTreasurer. The two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share\nanother. Passwords are passed down at Handover.
