The console runs only on a Co-VP's laptop (ADR-001), so they\n  would also need that laptop.\n- Co-VPs can set a new password for any Account. There is no \"forgot my\n  password\" email.\n- Deactivating is for a Position that is vacant, not for a person who has left.\n  A deactivated Account's Posts stay on the site, and Accounts are never deleted.\n- The last active Admin Account can never be deactivated or changed to Editor,\n  because with one shared Admin Account that would lock everyone out.\n- Moving to per-person Accounts later would mean re-deciding who the Author of\n  every existing Post is.\n"}},"serverClassifierRequest":"137818a8-764d-4994-bac6-d3404f87c5e1","apiBlockIndex":2,"requestId":"req_011CfbdRxsQ7N1vH7Cxo13Zo","type":"assistant","uuid":"a28dcb01-9f65-4881-9d47-8da2c4fdbbc1","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:53:41.413Z","advisorModel":"claude-opus-5-5","effort":"high","perTurnEffort":"high","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"a28dcb01-9f65-4881-9d47-8da2c4fdbbc1","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"838341c5-8e5b-4e73-a867-974a1a4ee26b","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01CejL5Ade7oMiiCh79ZRQVG","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-accounts-belong-to-positions.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"f014d5aa-6dd0-41a0-ae5c-971b67a7fe98","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:53:45.299Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/docs/adr/ADR-003-accounts-belong-to-positions.md","content":"# ADR-003: Accounts belong to Positions, not to people\n\n**Status:** accepted\n**Date:** 2026-10-01\n\n## Context\n\nAWM's Officers change every year. The client brief says \"there will be passwords\nthat are passed down from spring semester to fall semester each year.\" That can\nbe built two ways: one Account per Position, whose password is handed to\nwhoever holds the Position next, or one Account per person, created and\ndeactivated by the Co-VPs each year.\n\nPer-person Accounts are the usual choice, because a former Officer who still\nknows a shared password can still sign in. Per-Position Accounts were chosen\nanyway, for the client's stated reason: \"it isnt that top secret, former\nposition members will hardly think about it.\"\n\n## Decision\n\nThere is one Account per Position: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, and\nTreasurer. The two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share\nanother. Passwords are passed down at Handover. The Co-VP Account is the Admin;\nthe other three are Editors.\n\n## Consequences\n\n- The Author of a Post is a Position (\"Social Chair\"), never a named person. The\n  console cannot tell which of the two Co-VPs did something.\n- A former Officer who remembers a password can still sign in until a Co-VP\n  sets a new one. The console runs only on a Co-VP's laptop (ADR-001), so they\n  would also need that laptop.\n- Co-VPs can set a new password for any Account. There is no \"forgot my\n  password\" email.\n- Deactivating is for a Position that is vacant, not for a person who has left.\n  A deactivated Account's Posts stay on the site, and Accounts are never deleted.\n- The last active Admin Account can never be deactivated or changed to Editor,\n  because with one shared Admin Account that would lock everyone out.\n- Moving to per-person Accounts later would mean re-deciding who the Author of\n  every existing Post is.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"a28dcb01-9f65-4881-9d47-8da2c4fdbbc1","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"46840481-6a69-4536-aae5-ccc5eb0be163","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:53:45.503Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"**Handover**:","newString":"**Deactivated**:\nThe state of an Account whose Position is vacant. It cannot sign in, its Posts stay on the site, and it can be reactivated.\n_Avoid_: deleted, removed\n\n**Handover**:","originalFile":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. It belongs to the Position, not to a person, so the two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share another.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login\n\n**Role**:\nWhat an Account is allowed to do. There are two: Admin and Editor.\n\n**Admin**:\nThe Role of the Co-VPs, who maintain the site, create and delete Pages, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n\n**Editor**:\nThe Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page.\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's.\n\n**Visitor**:\nA member or curious student reading the public site. A Visitor never logs in.\n\n### Content\n\n**Study Hall**:\nAWM's weekly meeting.\n_Avoid_: meeting\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item on the site. It is the only kind of dated content.\n_Avoid_: announcement, update\n\n**Study Hall reminder**:\nThe weekly Monday Post about that night's Study Hall. Nearly every Post is one.\n\n**Author**:\nThe Position whose Account wrote a Post. Officers see it; Visitors do not.\n\n**Weekly email**:\nThe message Officers send by hand each week. Its text is the same as that week's Study Hall reminder, plus a link to the Post.\n\n**Page**:\nA permanent part of the site's structure. There are three: Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n\n**Home**:\nThe Page that holds the standing Study Hall time and place and shows the latest Published Post beneath it. Home always exists and is always Published.\n\n**Past posts**:\nThe list of older Published Posts that Visitors reach from Home. It is not a Page and no Officer creates it.\n\n### Publishing\n\n**Draft**:\nA Post or Page still being written, which Visitors cannot see.\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Officer gives a Post or Page when it is ready for Visitors. Published content reaches Visitors only at the next Go live.\n\n**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":27,"oldLines":6,"newStart":27,"newLines":10,"lines":[" **Editor**:"," The Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page."," ","+**Deactivated**:","+The state of an Account whose Position is vacant. It cannot sign in, its Posts stay on the site, and it can be reactivated.","+_Avoid_: deleted, removed","+"," **Handover**:"," The yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's."," "]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"061d8d00-d629-4d1e-a748-bcd0fe9c0bce","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

(file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"2373e6db-1405-41f6-81ab-480ccdf9b119","timestamp":"2026-10-01T13:53:45.705Z","toolUseResult":{"filePath":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms/CONTEXT.md","oldString":"**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export","newString":"**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n\n**Not live yet**:\nA change made since the last Go live, which Visitors therefore cannot see.\n\n**Link**:\nThe web address of a Post, made from its date and title. It stops changing once the Post is Published, so a Link sent in a Weekly email keeps working.\n_Avoid_: slug, permalink (in anything an Officer sees)","originalFile":"# AWM at Kenyon CMS\n\nThe website system AWM's Officers use to tell members and curious students when\nand where Study Hall is and how to join.\n\n## Language\n\n### People\n\n**Officer**:\nA student who currently holds a Position in AWM.\n\n**Position**:\nA named Officer job: Co-VP, Co-President, Social Chair, or Treasurer.\n_Avoid_: title, job\n\n**Account**:\nThe login for a Position, used by whoever holds that Position. It belongs to the Position, not to a person, so the two Co-VPs share one Account and the two Co-Presidents share another.\n_Avoid_: user, personal login\n\n**Role**:\nWhat an Account is allowed to do. There are two: Admin and Editor.\n\n**Admin**:\nThe Role of the Co-VPs, who maintain the site, create and delete Pages, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n\n**Editor**:\nThe Role of the Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer, who write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor never creates or deletes a Page.\n\n**Deactivated**:\nThe state of an Account whose Position is vacant. It cannot sign in, its Posts stay on the site, and it can be reactivated.\n_Avoid_: deleted, removed\n\n**Handover**:\nThe yearly passing of Account passwords from the spring semester's Officers to the fall semester's.\n\n**Visitor**:\nA member or curious student reading the public site. A Visitor never logs in.\n\n### Content\n\n**Study Hall**:\nAWM's weekly meeting.\n_Avoid_: meeting\n\n**Post**:\nA dated news item on the site. It is the only kind of dated content.\n_Avoid_: announcement, update\n\n**Study Hall reminder**:\nThe weekly Monday Post about that night's Study Hall. Nearly every Post is one.\n\n**Author**:\nThe Position whose Account wrote a Post. Officers see it; Visitors do not.\n\n**Weekly email**:\nThe message Officers send by hand each week. Its text is the same as that week's Study Hall reminder, plus a link to the Post.\n\n**Page**:\nA permanent part of the site's structure. There are three: Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n\n**Home**:\nThe Page that holds the standing Study Hall time and place and shows the latest Published Post beneath it. Home always exists and is always Published.\n\n**Past posts**:\nThe list of older Published Posts that Visitors reach from Home. It is not a Page and no Officer creates it.\n\n### Publishing\n\n**Draft**:\nA Post or Page still being written, which Visitors cannot see.\n\n**Published**:\nThe status an Officer gives a Post or Page when it is ready for Visitors. Published content reaches Visitors only at the next Go live.\n\n**Go live**:\nThe step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site.\n_Avoid_: deploy, export\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":76,"oldLines":3,"newStart":76,"newLines":10,"lines":[" **Go live**:"," The step, done by the Co-VPs, that puts everything Published onto the public site."," _Avoid_: deploy, export","+","+**Not live yet**:","+A change made since the last Go live, which Visitors therefore cannot see.","+","+**Link**:","+The web address of a Post, made from its date and title. It stops changing once the Post is Published, so a Link sent in a Weekly email keeps working.","+_Avoid_: slug, permalink (in anything an Officer sees)"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"783666af-4e90-4f49-ad7b-7010044a965f","session_id":"0bec5f8c-6b9c-4a75-b2f2-851783fcd0ab","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

It only counts if the base score is already 70 or more, and it needs its own `stretch` issue, passing tests, and a review comment. Three ways to do photos:\n\n- **(a) Upload in the console.** An officer picks a photo file while editing a page. This is the stretch goal: file storage, a new screen, and Go live has to copy the files.\n- **(b) Link to a photo hosted elsewhere.** An officer pastes the web address of a photo into the page text. No upload feature, but the photo disappears if the other site removes it, and an officer has to learn the Markdown image syntax.\n- **(c) No photos by Tuesday.** About is names and positions in text.\n\nScenario: at Handover in the fall, the new Co-VPs have to replace six officer photos. Under (a) they do it in the console; under (b) they first have to put the photos somewhere public and copy six addresses.\n\n➡️ **(c) for the seven required capabilities, then (a) as a stretch ticket at the end of the list**, built only after all seven are working. Any Editor can write, publish, and permanently delete any post after a confirmation.\n- **Page:** three permanent ones: Home, About, Join & Snacks. Only Co-VPs create, delete, or change a page's status. Editors edit text only. Home cannot be deleted or unpublished and shows the standing time and room plus the latest post.\n- **Who may do what:** four accounts, one per position. Co-VP is Admin; Co-President, Social Chair, and Treasurer are Editors. Co-VPs manage accounts, set passwords, and deactivate vacant positions. The last Admin can't be removed.\n- **Publishing:** an officer marks content Published; a Co-VP presses Go live on the one laptop. The dashboard warns when changes are not live yet. {"parentUuid":"41c25022-eccd-4459-9b56-e7bcf0d023e5","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1eb4ba8e-c18e-4e70-9e6f-37b30a51517c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Base directory for this skill: /home/msgre/.claude/plugins/cache/claude-plugins-official/mattpocock-skills/1.2.3/skills/engineering/to-spec\n\nThis skill takes the current conversation context and codebase understanding and produces a spec. Do NOT interview the user; just synthesize what you already know.\n\nThe issue tracker and triage label vocabulary should have been provided to you. If not, tell the user to run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`.\n\n## Process\n\n1. Explore the repo to understand the current state of the codebase, if you haven't already. Use the project's domain glossary vocabulary throughout the spec, and respect any ADRs in the area you're touching.\n\n2. Sketch out the seams at which you're going to test the feature. Existing seams should be preferred to new ones. Use the highest seam possible. If new seams are needed, propose them at the highest point you can. The fewer seams across the codebase, the better - the ideal number is one.\n\nCheck with the user that these seams match their expectations.\n\n3. Write the spec using the template below, then publish it to the project issue tracker. Apply the `ready-for-agent` triage label - no need for additional triage.\n\n<spec-template>\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nThe problem that the user is facing, from the user's perspective.\n\n## Solution\n\nThe solution to the problem, from the user's perspective.\n\n## User Stories\n\nA LONG, numbered list of user stories. Each user story should be in the format of:\n\n1. As an <actor>, I want a <feature>, so that <benefit>\n\n<user-story-example>\n1. As a mobile bank customer, I want to see balance on my accounts, so that I can make better informed decisions about my spending\n</user-story-example>\n\nThis list of user stories should be extremely extensive and cover all aspects of the feature.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\nA list of implementation decisions that were made. This can include:\n\n- The modules that will be built/modified\n- The interfaces of those modules that will be modified\n- Technical clarifications from the developer\n- Architectural decisions\n- Schema changes\n- API contracts\n- Specific interactions\n\nDo NOT include specific file paths or code snippets. They may end up being outdated very quickly.\n\nException: if a prototype produced a snippet that encodes a decision more precisely than prose can (state machine, reducer, schema, type shape), inline it within the relevant decision and note briefly that it came from a prototype. Trim to the decision-rich parts, not a working demo, just the important bits.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA list of testing decisions that were made. Include:\n\n- A description of what makes a good test (only test external behavior, not implementation details)\n- Which modules will be tested\n- Prior art for the tests (i.e. similar types of tests in the codebase)\n\n## Out of Scope\n\nA description of the things that are out of scope for this spec.\n\n## Further Notes\n\nAny further notes about the feature.\n\n</spec-template>\n"}]},"isMeta":true,"turnCompanion":true,"uuid":"149f4d8e-231a-4b62-b49e-65fb743e2bc4","timestamp":"2026-10-01T14:08:51.684Z","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/home/msgre/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd","version":"2.1.286","gitBranch":"main"}

{"parentUuid":"a5d67e4d-3f54-415e-88ec-104c8326c74a","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1eb4ba8e-c18e-4e70-9e6f-37b30a51517c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01HLUeCkxUZQW72GaVnL3dPU","type":"tool_result","content":"spec\n=== issue-tracker\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). GitHub reports `issue_dependencies_summary.blocked_by` (open blockers only, the live gate). Where dependencies aren't available, fall back to a `Blocked by: #<n>, #<n>` line at the top of the child body. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\n- **Child ticket**: an issue linked to the map as a GitHub sub-issue (`gh api` on the sub-issues endpoint). Where sub-issues aren't enabled, add the child to a task list in the map body and put `Part of #<map>` at the top of the child body. Labels: `wayfinder:<type>` (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`). Once claimed, the ticket is assigned to the driving dev.\n- **Blocking**: GitHub's **native issue dependencies**, the canonical, UI-visible representation. Add an edge with `gh api --method POST repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<child>/dependencies/blocked_by -F issue_id=<blocker-db-id>`, where `<blocker-db-id>` is the blocker's numeric **database id** (`gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> --jq .id`, _not_ the `#number` or `node_id`). {"parentUuid":"e5730b83-564f-407b-b4e3-1b16e658a6c7","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011CfbeiaNQFZqeoWoSh49Tu","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_019cKKYHDM8LH3efKRoFzioP","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-msgre-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"Vocabulary in this spec follows `CONTEXT.md`. Decisions it builds on: ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Accounts belong to Positions).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nAWM at Kenyon runs a weekly Study Hall (Mondays 8–10pm, Hayes 311) and its Officers want members and curious students to be able to find out when and where it is and how to join.\n\nToday the site is raw HTML. Changing anything means editing HTML by hand, and the Study Hall time and place is written in three separate files, so a change has to be made three times. Because of that, the Weekly email is the only way AWM actually communicates.\n\nThe Officers change every year and each new Officer has a different level of computing experience. A site that needs HTML does not survive a Handover.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS that the Officers use on one Co-VP's laptop, which produces the public AWM site.\n\n- An Officer signs in with their Position's Account, writes the Monday Study Hall reminder as a Post in plain text, and marks it Published. No HTML.\n- The standing Study Hall time and place lives in exactly one place: the Home Page. Home also shows the latest Published Post.\n- A Co-VP presses **Go live**, and the public site is updated. The Officer then sends the Weekly email by hand, with the same text plus the Post's Link.\n- The Co-VPs are Admins: they maintain the three Pages (Home, About, Join & Snacks), manage Accounts, and Go live. The Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer are Editors: they write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor can never create, delete, or unpublish a Page.\n\n### Who uses it\n\n- **Visitors** (members and curious students) read the public site. They never sign in.\n- **Editors** (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer Accounts) post the Study Hall reminder and other news.\n- **Admins** (the Co-VP Account) run the site.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, in AWM's words\n\n1. **Login.** Each Position's Account signs in and out of the console. Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes.\n2. **Two roles.** Admin (Co-VP) and Editor (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer), with different permissions enforced in code.\n3. **Posts.** Officers create, read, update, and delete Posts: title, Link, Markdown body, Draft/Published, Author (a Position), and timestamps.\n4. **Pages.** Home, About, and Join & Snacks, with the same fields. Published Pages make up the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts and the Go live status, one content list that filters by status and type, and an editor with a preview.\n6. **Account management.** Admin only: create an Account for a Position, change its Role, set its password, and deactivate it. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in.\n7. **Public site and Go live.** Only Published content, sanitized Markdown, navigation built from Pages, and `cms publish` writing `site/` with relative paths. Go live is the button that runs it and pushes the result.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Visitors\n\n1. As a curious student, I want to see when and where Study Hall is on the Home Page, so that I can show up without asking anyone.\n2. As a member, I want to see the latest Post in full on the Home Page, so that I know what is happening this week.\n3. As a member, I want every Post to show its date with the weekday, so that I know which Monday \"tonight\" refers to.\n4. As a member, I want a Past posts list, so that I can find an older Post.\n5. As a member who clicked the Link in the Weekly email, I want to land on that exact Post, so that the email and the site agree.\n6. As a member, I want a Link from an old email to keep working, so that I never hit a dead page.\n7. As a curious student, I want an About Page describing AWM and its Officers, so that I know who runs it.\n8. As a curious student, I want a Join & Snacks Page with the Google Form link, so that I can join or request snacks.\n9. As a Visitor, I want the same navigation on every public page, so that I can move between Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n10. As a Visitor, I want never to see a Draft, so that I only read what the Officers meant to publish.\n11. As a Visitor on a phone, I want the site to fit my screen, so that I can check the room on the way to Hayes.\n12. As a Visitor, I want Posts to read as coming from AWM with no individual name, so that it matches the Weekly email.\n\n### Signing in\n\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Position's Account, so that I can use the console.\n14. As an Officer, I want to sign out, so that the next Officer at the laptop does not act as my Position.\n15. As an Officer, I want to be signed out when the browser closes, so that a forgotten sign-out does not leave the Account open.\n16. As an Officer who mistypes, I want a clear \"wrong email or password\" message, so that I can try again.\n17. As a Co-VP, I want that message to be the same whether or not the Account exists, so that it gives nothing away.\n18. As a Co-VP, I want anyone who is not signed in to be sent to the sign-in screen, so that no console screen is visible without an Account.\n\n### Editors and Posts\n\n19. As a new Officer, I want to write the Study Hall reminder in a plain text box, so that I never have to learn HTML.\n20. As an Editor, I want a short hint under the text box showing how to make bold text and a link, so that I can add the Google Form link without looking anything up.\n21. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n22. As an Editor, I want to preview a Post before I publish it, so that I can see what Visitors will see.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it goes out at the next Go live.\n24. As an Editor, I want the Post's Link to be made for me from the date and title, so that I never have to type one.\n25. As an Editor, I want two reminders with the same title to get different Links, so that every week's Post has its own address.\n26. As an Editor, I want to fix a typo in a Published Post without its Link changing, so that the email link still works.\n27. As an Editor, I want to set a Post back to Draft, so that I can pull something published by mistake.\n28. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including one written by another Position, so that whoever is at the laptop can fix it.\n29. As an Editor, I want to delete any Post after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that a cancelled or wrong Post can be removed.\n30. As an Editor, I want to post things other than the weekly reminder (a cancelled Study Hall, a snack update), so that all news goes through one kind of Post.\n31. As an Editor, I want a message after every save, publish, or delete saying what happened, so that I know it worked.\n32. As an Editor, I want to see the Post's public address once it is live, so that I can copy it into the Weekly email.\n\n### Editors and Pages\n\n33. As an Editor, I want to edit the text of an existing Page, so that I can update the Study Hall room or the Officer list.\n34. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to create a Page, so that nobody adds to the navigation by accident.\n35. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to delete a Page, so that the site's structure is safe.\n36. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to change a Page's status, so that a Page cannot vanish from the navigation.\n37. As an Editor who types an Admin-only address directly, I want a clear \"no permission\" screen, so that I know it is not broken.\n\n### Co-VPs (Admins)\n\n38. As a Co-VP, I want to create a Page, so that the site can grow when AWM needs it to.\n39. As a Co-VP, I want to delete a Page other than Home after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that I can remove one we no longer need.\n40. As a Co-VP, I want to set a Page to Draft or Published, so that I control what is in the navigation.\n41. As a Co-VP, I want Home to be impossible to delete or unpublish, so that the site always has a front page.\n42. As a Co-VP, I want to change the Study Hall time or room in one place, so that it is never out of date in a second file.\n43. As a Co-VP, I want a Go live button, so that I can update the public site without a terminal.\n44. As a Co-VP, I want the dashboard to show when the last Go live was, so that I know how current the public site is.\n45. As a Co-VP, I want a warning with the number of changes that are Not live yet, so that a Published reminder is never left unseen.\n46. As a Co-VP, I want a plain error if Go live fails, so that I know the public site did not change.\n47. As a Co-VP, I want Editors not to have the Go live button, so that going public stays with us.\n48. As a Co-VP, I want to see every Account with its Position, Role, and whether it is Deactivated, so that I know who can sign in.\n49. As a Co-VP, I want to create an Account for a new Position and choose its Role, so that a new Officer job can post.\n50. As a Co-VP, I want to change an Account's Role, so that a Position's permissions can change.\n51. As a Co-VP, I want to set a new password for any Account, so that a forgotten password or a Handover is a one-minute fix.\n52. As a Co-VP, I want to deactivate the Account of a vacant Position, so that it cannot sign in.\n53. As a Co-VP, I want to reactivate an Account, so that a Position that returns can post again.\n54. As a Co-VP, I want a Deactivated Account's Posts to stay on the site, so that history is not lost.\n55. As a Co-VP, I want the console to refuse to deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so that we cannot lock ourselves out.\n\n### Everyone in the console\n\n56. As an Officer, I want a dashboard with counts of Draft Posts, Published Posts, and Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n57. As an Officer, I want one content list of Posts and Pages, newest first, so that I can find anything.\n58. As an Officer, I want to filter that list by Draft/Published and by Post/Page, so that I can find last week's reminder quickly.\n59. As an Officer, I want the list to show each Post's Author as a Position, so that I know which Position wrote it.\n60. As an Officer, I want the same navigation on every console screen, so that I never get lost.\n61. As an Officer on a phone-width window, I want console screens not to scroll sideways, so that they stay usable.\n\n### Running and grading\n\n62. As the developer, I want a seed command that creates the demo Accounts, the three Pages, and a few Posts (at least one Draft, one Published), so that the CMS can be used immediately from a clean clone.\n63. It is called by the dashboard button and by the `cms deploy` command.\n- **Admin console.** Dashboard, content list, editor, Accounts screen, sign-in screen. Server-rendered templates, no JavaScript framework (ADR-002).\n- **Seed script.** Extended to create demo Accounts, Pages, and Posts.\n\n### Data\n\n- **Account:** sign-in email (unique), display name (the Position, e.g. \"Social Chair\"), password hash, Role (`admin` or `editor`), active flag, created time.\n- **Post:** title, Link (unique among Posts), Markdown body, status (`draft` or `published`), Author (an Account), created time, updated time, first-published time.\n- **Page:** the same fields, plus a marker for which Page is Home.\n- **Site state:** the time of the last Go live, and a count of changes that are Not live yet.\n- Storage is SQLite (ADR-002). Admins: everything Editors can do, plus create and delete Pages, change a Page's title and status, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n- **Home.** Created automatically if missing. Cannot be deleted or set to Draft by anyone. Its body holds the standing Study Hall time and place.\n- **Links.** A Post's Link is the date plus a URL-safe form of the title (for example `2026-10-05-study-hall-tonight`). If that Link already exists, a number is added. A Page's Link is the URL-safe form of its title. A Link is set when the item is first Published and never changes after that, even if the title changes or the item goes back to Draft and is Published again. Officers never type a Link.\n- **Dates.** A Post's public date is its first-published time, shown with the weekday. Dates are shown in US Eastern time.\n- **Deleting.** Deleting a Post or Page is permanent and always goes through a confirmation screen. There is no trash.\n- **Accounts.** Accounts are deactivated, never deleted. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in, and an existing session for it stops working. The last active Admin cannot be deactivated or changed to Editor.\n- **Passwords.** Only an Admin sets a password, from the Accounts screen. No password is ever logged or shown.\n- **Not live yet.** Any change that would alter the public site adds one to the count: publishing or unpublishing, editing or deleting something Published. Edits to Drafts do not count. Go live resets the count to zero.\n- **Go live.** Admin only. If the push fails, the console shows a plain error, and the count and last Go live time are left as they were.\n\n### Contracts\n\n- Sign-in is a form posted to `/login` with fields `email` and `password`, matching the template's test helper. The console lives under `/admin`.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token, including sign-out, delete, and Go live. A POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- An anonymous request to any console screen redirects to sign-in. A signed-in Editor requesting an Admin-only screen gets a 403 \"no permission\" screen.\n- Wrong email and wrong password give the same message.\n- `/` on the local app is a preview of the public site and shows Published content only.\n\n### Public site layout\n\n- Home at the site root; one file per other Published Page; one file per Published Post in a posts folder; a Past posts list in that folder; one stylesheet.\n- Navigation: Home first, then the other Published Pages in the order they were created. Past posts is linked from Home, not from the navigation.\n- Home shows its own body, then the latest Published Post in full. Past posts lists the older Published Posts, newest first.\n- Every `href` and `src` is relative. Files in the posts folder reach the stylesheet and the Pages with `../`.\n- No Author is shown publicly.\n- Raw HTML typed into a body is not passed through, and the rendered HTML is sanitized with an allowlist. Images are not in the allowlist.\n\n### Demo data\n\n- The seed creates four Accounts: Co-VP (Admin), and Co-President, Social Chair, and Treasurer (Editors). The Co-VP signs in as `admin@example.test` and the Social Chair as `editor@example.test`, matching the template's test helper; the other two use `copresident@example.test` and `treasurer@example.test`.\n- Passwords come from the environment. All three Editor Accounts use the one Editor demo password.\n- The seed creates Home, About, and Join & Snacks as Published Pages, and at least one Published and one Draft Post.\n\n### Screens\n\n- Every console screen has the same navigation and shows a success or error message after each action.\n- The editor has a formatting hint under the body box (bold, link) and a Preview button that shows the sanitized rendering.\n- Once a Post is live, the editor shows its full public address, built from the configured public site address.\n- No horizontal scrolling at 390 px on the public Home page or the console screens.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test here drives the app the way an Officer or Visitor does and checks what they would see: a status code, a redirect, text on a screen, or a file in the exported site. Tests do not reach into the database or call internal functions to check how something was stored.\n\n### Seams\n\nThere are two seams, and both already exist in the template.\n\n1. **The console over HTTP.** Tests use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures to request screens and post forms. This covers sign-in, Roles, Posts, Pages, the dashboard, the content list, preview, Accounts, CSRF, and Go live.\n2. **The exported site.** Tests call the export into a temporary folder and read the files it wrote. This covers Published-only content, navigation, relative paths, sanitizing, dates, and Links.\n\nOne thing is replaced in tests: the push to GitHub inside Go live. Tests swap it for a fake that records it was called (or fails on purpose), so no test ever pushes to the real repository.\n\nEach test runs against its own temporary database seeded with the demo Accounts, so the fixed test passwords in the fixtures work.\n\n### What gets tested\n\n- Every row of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` has at least one test.\n- Each Role rule has a test for the allowed case and the refused case, requested by direct URL rather than by clicking.\n- Draft content never appears in the export, the local preview, or the Past posts list.\n- A body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute is harmless in both the preview and the export.\n- Link rules: same-title collision, frozen after Published.\n- Last-Admin protection, Home protection, Deactivated sign-in refusal.\n- Not live yet count goes up on public-affecting changes and resets on Go live; a failed push leaves it unchanged.\n\n### Prior art\n\n`tests/test_t00.py` already uses both seams. Its four tests are kept. One must change when sign-in lands: it currently expects an anonymous request to `/admin` to return the \"hello admin\" page, which contradicts the rule that anonymous Visitors are redirected to sign-in. It becomes two assertions: anonymous is redirected, and a signed-in Officer sees the dashboard.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Sending the Weekly email. It stays manual; the CMS only supplies the Link.\n- Hosting the snack request form. Join & Snacks links to the Google Form.\n- Scheduled Posts or a calendar.\n- Comments, or any Visitor sign-in.\n- Image uploads, including Officer photos on About, and images linked from other sites. A console upload for Pages with alt text may be added later as a separate `stretch` issue, only after all seven capabilities work.\n- Categories, tags, and search.\n- A trash bin or undo for deleted Posts.\n- \"Forgot my password\" emails.\n- A \"copy last week's reminder\" button. This is the first future improvement.\n- One Account per person (see ADR-003).\n- Putting the console on the internet (see ADR-001).\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and rich-text editors (excluded by the assignment).\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Stage 2 is due Tuesday Oct 6, 2:40 pm, with grace to Wednesday Oct 7, 2:40 pm. In this project, **Published** is a status and **Go live** is the step that reaches Visitors. The `cms publish` command keeps its name because the assignment fixes it; it is the export half of Go live.\n- The Accounts screen is what the assignment calls \"user management\". Decisions it builds on: ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Accounts belong to Positions).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nAWM at Kenyon runs a weekly Study Hall (Mondays 8–10pm, Hayes 311) and its Officers want members and curious students to be able to find out when and where it is and how to join.\n\nToday the site is raw HTML. Changing anything means editing HTML by hand, and the Study Hall time and place is written in three separate files, so a change has to be made three times. Because of that, the Weekly email is the only way AWM actually communicates.\n\nThe Officers change every year and each new Officer has a different level of computing experience. A site that needs HTML does not survive a Handover.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS that the Officers use on one Co-VP's laptop, which produces the public AWM site.\n\n- An Officer signs in with their Position's Account, writes the Monday Study Hall reminder as a Post in plain text, and marks it Published. No HTML.\n- The standing Study Hall time and place lives in exactly one place: the Home Page. Home also shows the latest Published Post.\n- A Co-VP presses **Go live**, and the public site is updated. The Officer then sends the Weekly email by hand, with the same text plus the Post's Link.\n- The Co-VPs are Admins: they maintain the three Pages (Home, About, Join & Snacks), manage Accounts, and Go live. The Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer are Editors: they write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor can never create, delete, or unpublish a Page.\n\n### Who uses it\n\n- **Visitors** (members and curious students) read the public site. They never sign in.\n- **Editors** (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer Accounts) post the Study Hall reminder and other news.\n- **Admins** (the Co-VP Account) run the site.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, in AWM's words\n\n1. **Login.** Each Position's Account signs in and out of the console. Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes.\n2. **Two roles.** Admin (Co-VP) and Editor (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer), with different permissions enforced in code.\n3. **Posts.** Officers create, read, update, and delete Posts: title, Link, Markdown body, Draft/Published, Author (a Position), and timestamps.\n4. **Pages.** Home, About, and Join & Snacks, with the same fields. Published Pages make up the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts and the Go live status, one content list that filters by status and type, and an editor with a preview.\n6. **Account management.** Admin only: create an Account for a Position, change its Role, set its password, and deactivate it. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in.\n7. **Public site and Go live.** Only Published content, sanitized Markdown, navigation built from Pages, and `cms publish` writing `site/` with relative paths. Go live is the button that runs it and pushes the result.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Visitors\n\n1. As a curious student, I want to see when and where Study Hall is on the Home Page, so that I can show up without asking anyone.\n2. As a member, I want to see the latest Post in full on the Home Page, so that I know what is happening this week.\n3. As a member, I want every Post to show its date with the weekday, so that I know which Monday \"tonight\" refers to.\n4. As a member, I want a Past posts list, so that I can find an older Post.\n5. As a member who clicked the Link in the Weekly email, I want to land on that exact Post, so that the email and the site agree.\n6. As a member, I want a Link from an old email to keep working, so that I never hit a dead page.\n7. As a curious student, I want an About Page describing AWM and its Officers, so that I know who runs it.\n8. As a curious student, I want a Join & Snacks Page with the Google Form link, so that I can join or request snacks.\n9. As a Visitor, I want the same navigation on every public page, so that I can move between Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n10. As a Visitor, I want never to see a Draft, so that I only read what the Officers meant to publish.\n11. As a Visitor on a phone, I want the site to fit my screen, so that I can check the room on the way to Hayes.\n12. As a Visitor, I want Posts to read as coming from AWM with no individual name, so that it matches the Weekly email.\n\n### Signing in\n\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Position's Account, so that I can use the console.\n14. As an Officer, I want to sign out, so that the next Officer at the laptop does not act as my Position.\n15. As an Officer, I want to be signed out when the browser closes, so that a forgotten sign-out does not leave the Account open.\n16. As an Officer who mistypes, I want a clear \"wrong email or password\" message, so that I can try again.\n17. As a Co-VP, I want that message to be the same whether or not the Account exists, so that it gives nothing away.\n18. As a Co-VP, I want anyone who is not signed in to be sent to the sign-in screen, so that no console screen is visible without an Account.\n\n### Editors and Posts\n\n19. As a new Officer, I want to write the Study Hall reminder in a plain text box, so that I never have to learn HTML.\n20. As an Editor, I want a short hint under the text box showing how to make bold text and a link, so that I can add the Google Form link without looking anything up.\n21. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n22. As an Editor, I want to preview a Post before I publish it, so that I can see what Visitors will see.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it goes out at the next Go live.\n24. As an Editor, I want the Post's Link to be made for me from the date and title, so that I never have to type one.\n25. Past posts is linked from Home, not from the navigation.\n- Home shows its own body, then the latest Published Post in full. Past posts lists the older Published Posts, newest first.\n- Every `href` and `src` is relative. Files in the posts folder reach the stylesheet and the Pages with `../`.\n- No Author is shown publicly.\n- Raw HTML typed into a body is not passed through, and the rendered HTML is sanitized with an allowlist. Images are not in the allowlist.\n\n### Demo data\n\n- The seed creates four Accounts: Co-VP (Admin), and Co-President, Social Chair, and Treasurer (Editors). The Co-VP signs in as `admin@example.test` and the Social Chair as `editor@example.test`, matching the template's test helper; the other two use `copresident@example.test` and `treasurer@example.test`.\n- Passwords come from the environment. All three Editor Accounts use the one Editor demo password.\n- The seed creates Home, About, and Join & Snacks as Published Pages, and at least one Published and one Draft Post.\n\n### Screens\n\n- Every console screen has the same navigation and shows a success or error message after each action.\n- The editor has a formatting hint under the body box (bold, link) and a Preview button that shows the sanitized rendering.\n- Once a Post is live, the editor shows its full public address, built from the configured public site address.\n- No horizontal scrolling at 390 px on the public Home page or the console screens.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test here drives the app the way an Officer or Visitor does and checks what they would see: a status code, a redirect, text on a screen, or a file in the exported site. Tests do not reach into the database or call internal functions to check how something was stored.\n\n### Seams\n\nThere are two seams, and both already exist in the template.\n\n1. **The console over HTTP.** Tests use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures to request screens and post forms. This covers sign-in, Roles, Posts, Pages, the dashboard, the content list, preview, Accounts, CSRF, and Go live.\n2. **The exported site.** Tests call the export into a temporary folder and read the files it wrote. This covers Published-only content, navigation, relative paths, sanitizing, dates, and Links.\n\nOne thing is replaced in tests: the push to GitHub inside Go live. Tests swap it for a fake that records it was called (or fails on purpose), so no test ever pushes to the real repository.\n\nEach test runs against its own temporary database seeded with the demo Accounts, so the fixed test passwords in the fixtures work.\n\n### What gets tested\n\n- Every row of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` has at least one test.\n- Each Role rule has a test for the allowed case and the refused case, requested by direct URL rather than by clicking.\n- Draft content never appears in the export, the local preview, or the Past posts list.\n- A body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute is harmless in both the preview and the export.\n- Link rules: same-title collision, frozen after Published.\n- Last-Admin protection, Home protection, Deactivated sign-in refusal.\n- Not live yet count goes up on public-affecting changes and resets on Go live; a failed push leaves it unchanged.\n\n### Prior art\n\n`tests/test_t00.py` already uses both seams. Its four tests are kept. One must change when sign-in lands: it currently expects an anonymous request to `/admin` to return the \"hello admin\" page, which contradicts the rule that anonymous Visitors are redirected to sign-in. It becomes two assertions: anonymous is redirected, and a signed-in Officer sees the dashboard.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Sending the Weekly email. It stays manual; the CMS only supplies the Link.\n- Hosting the snack request form. Join & Snacks links to the Google Form.\n- Scheduled Posts or a calendar.\n- Comments, or any Visitor sign-in.\n- Image uploads, including Officer photos on About, and images linked from other sites. A console upload for Pages with alt text may be added later as a separate `stretch` issue, only after all seven capabilities work.\n- Categories, tags, and search.\n- A trash bin or undo for deleted Posts.\n- \"Forgot my password\" emails.\n- A \"copy last week's reminder\" button. This is the first future improvement.\n- One Account per person (see ADR-003).\n- Putting the console on the internet (see ADR-001).\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and rich-text editors (excluded by the assignment).\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Stage 2 is due Tuesday Oct 6, 2:40 pm, with grace to Wednesday Oct 7, 2:40 pm. Tickets should be ordered so sign-in, Posts, and the export land first.\n- The Monday routine this spec is built around: an Officer writes the Study Hall reminder, marks it Published, a Co-VP presses Go live, and the Officer sends the Weekly email with the Link.\n- \"Publish\" means two different things in everyday speech. In this project, **Published** is a status and **Go live** is the step that reaches Visitors. The `cms publish` command keeps its name because the assignment fixes it; it is the export half of Go live.\n- The Accounts screen is what the assignment calls \"user management\". {"parentUuid":"b63f33ab-43c3-46fc-a098-61bf1697509d","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"1eb4ba8e-c18e-4e70-9e6f-37b30a51517c","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019cKKYHDM8LH3efKRoFzioP","type":"tool_result","content":"File created successfully at: /tmp/claude-1000/-home-msgre-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd/scratchpad/spec.md (file state is current in your context — no need to Read it back)"}]},"uuid":"4fbda1a9-ad03-4d09-a3a9-23eef03c5921","timestamp":"2026-10-01T14:11:23.929Z","toolUseResult":{"type":"create","filePath":"/tmp/claude-1000/-home-msgre-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd/scratchpad/spec.md","content":"Vocabulary in this spec follows `CONTEXT.md`. Decisions it builds on: ADR-001 (local admin console, static public site), ADR-002 (stack), ADR-003 (Accounts belong to Positions).\n\n## Problem Statement\n\nAWM at Kenyon runs a weekly Study Hall (Mondays 8–10pm, Hayes 311) and its Officers want members and curious students to be able to find out when and where it is and how to join.\n\nToday the site is raw HTML. Changing anything means editing HTML by hand, and the Study Hall time and place is written in three separate files, so a change has to be made three times. Because of that, the Weekly email is the only way AWM actually communicates.\n\nThe Officers change every year and each new Officer has a different level of computing experience. A site that needs HTML does not survive a Handover.\n\n## Solution\n\nA small CMS that the Officers use on one Co-VP's laptop, which produces the public AWM site.\n\n- An Officer signs in with their Position's Account, writes the Monday Study Hall reminder as a Post in plain text, and marks it Published. No HTML.\n- The standing Study Hall time and place lives in exactly one place: the Home Page. Home also shows the latest Published Post.\n- A Co-VP presses **Go live**, and the public site is updated. The Officer then sends the Weekly email by hand, with the same text plus the Post's Link.\n- The Co-VPs are Admins: they maintain the three Pages (Home, About, Join & Snacks), manage Accounts, and Go live. The Co-Presidents, Social Chair, and Treasurer are Editors: they write, publish, and delete Posts and edit the text of existing Pages. An Editor can never create, delete, or unpublish a Page.\n\n### Who uses it\n\n- **Visitors** (members and curious students) read the public site. They never sign in.\n- **Editors** (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer Accounts) post the Study Hall reminder and other news.\n- **Admins** (the Co-VP Account) run the site.\n\n### The seven required capabilities, in AWM's words\n\n1. **Login.** Each Position's Account signs in and out of the console. Passwords are stored as argon2 hashes.\n2. **Two roles.** Admin (Co-VP) and Editor (Co-President, Social Chair, Treasurer), with different permissions enforced in code.\n3. **Posts.** Officers create, read, update, and delete Posts: title, Link, Markdown body, Draft/Published, Author (a Position), and timestamps.\n4. **Pages.** Home, About, and Join & Snacks, with the same fields. Published Pages make up the public navigation.\n5. **Admin console.** A dashboard with counts and the Go live status, one content list that filters by status and type, and an editor with a preview.\n6. **Account management.** Admin only: create an Account for a Position, change its Role, set its password, and deactivate it. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in.\n7. **Public site and Go live.** Only Published content, sanitized Markdown, navigation built from Pages, and `cms publish` writing `site/` with relative paths. Go live is the button that runs it and pushes the result.\n\n## User Stories\n\n### Visitors\n\n1. As a curious student, I want to see when and where Study Hall is on the Home Page, so that I can show up without asking anyone.\n2. As a member, I want to see the latest Post in full on the Home Page, so that I know what is happening this week.\n3. As a member, I want every Post to show its date with the weekday, so that I know which Monday \"tonight\" refers to.\n4. As a member, I want a Past posts list, so that I can find an older Post.\n5. As a member who clicked the Link in the Weekly email, I want to land on that exact Post, so that the email and the site agree.\n6. As a member, I want a Link from an old email to keep working, so that I never hit a dead page.\n7. As a curious student, I want an About Page describing AWM and its Officers, so that I know who runs it.\n8. As a curious student, I want a Join & Snacks Page with the Google Form link, so that I can join or request snacks.\n9. As a Visitor, I want the same navigation on every public page, so that I can move between Home, About, and Join & Snacks.\n10. As a Visitor, I want never to see a Draft, so that I only read what the Officers meant to publish.\n11. As a Visitor on a phone, I want the site to fit my screen, so that I can check the room on the way to Hayes.\n12. As a Visitor, I want Posts to read as coming from AWM with no individual name, so that it matches the Weekly email.\n\n### Signing in\n\n13. As an Officer, I want to sign in with my Position's Account, so that I can use the console.\n14. As an Officer, I want to sign out, so that the next Officer at the laptop does not act as my Position.\n15. As an Officer, I want to be signed out when the browser closes, so that a forgotten sign-out does not leave the Account open.\n16. As an Officer who mistypes, I want a clear \"wrong email or password\" message, so that I can try again.\n17. As a Co-VP, I want that message to be the same whether or not the Account exists, so that it gives nothing away.\n18. As a Co-VP, I want anyone who is not signed in to be sent to the sign-in screen, so that no console screen is visible without an Account.\n\n### Editors and Posts\n\n19. As a new Officer, I want to write the Study Hall reminder in a plain text box, so that I never have to learn HTML.\n20. As an Editor, I want a short hint under the text box showing how to make bold text and a link, so that I can add the Google Form link without looking anything up.\n21. As an Editor, I want to save a Post as a Draft, so that I can finish it later.\n22. As an Editor, I want to preview a Post before I publish it, so that I can see what Visitors will see.\n23. As an Editor, I want to mark a Post Published, so that it goes out at the next Go live.\n24. As an Editor, I want the Post's Link to be made for me from the date and title, so that I never have to type one.\n25. As an Editor, I want two reminders with the same title to get different Links, so that every week's Post has its own address.\n26. As an Editor, I want to fix a typo in a Published Post without its Link changing, so that the email link still works.\n27. As an Editor, I want to set a Post back to Draft, so that I can pull something published by mistake.\n28. As an Editor, I want to edit any Post, including one written by another Position, so that whoever is at the laptop can fix it.\n29. As an Editor, I want to delete any Post after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that a cancelled or wrong Post can be removed.\n30. As an Editor, I want to post things other than the weekly reminder (a cancelled Study Hall, a snack update), so that all news goes through one kind of Post.\n31. As an Editor, I want a message after every save, publish, or delete saying what happened, so that I know it worked.\n32. As an Editor, I want to see the Post's public address once it is live, so that I can copy it into the Weekly email.\n\n### Editors and Pages\n\n33. As an Editor, I want to edit the text of an existing Page, so that I can update the Study Hall room or the Officer list.\n34. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to create a Page, so that nobody adds to the navigation by accident.\n35. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to delete a Page, so that the site's structure is safe.\n36. As a Co-VP, I want an Editor to be unable to change a Page's status, so that a Page cannot vanish from the navigation.\n37. As an Editor who types an Admin-only address directly, I want a clear \"no permission\" screen, so that I know it is not broken.\n\n### Co-VPs (Admins)\n\n38. As a Co-VP, I want to create a Page, so that the site can grow when AWM needs it to.\n39. As a Co-VP, I want to delete a Page other than Home after an \"Are you sure?\" step, so that I can remove one we no longer need.\n40. As a Co-VP, I want to set a Page to Draft or Published, so that I control what is in the navigation.\n41. As a Co-VP, I want Home to be impossible to delete or unpublish, so that the site always has a front page.\n42. As a Co-VP, I want to change the Study Hall time or room in one place, so that it is never out of date in a second file.\n43. As a Co-VP, I want a Go live button, so that I can update the public site without a terminal.\n44. As a Co-VP, I want the dashboard to show when the last Go live was, so that I know how current the public site is.\n45. As a Co-VP, I want a warning with the number of changes that are Not live yet, so that a Published reminder is never left unseen.\n46. As a Co-VP, I want a plain error if Go live fails, so that I know the public site did not change.\n47. As a Co-VP, I want Editors not to have the Go live button, so that going public stays with us.\n48. As a Co-VP, I want to see every Account with its Position, Role, and whether it is Deactivated, so that I know who can sign in.\n49. As a Co-VP, I want to create an Account for a new Position and choose its Role, so that a new Officer job can post.\n50. As a Co-VP, I want to change an Account's Role, so that a Position's permissions can change.\n51. As a Co-VP, I want to set a new password for any Account, so that a forgotten password or a Handover is a one-minute fix.\n52. As a Co-VP, I want to deactivate the Account of a vacant Position, so that it cannot sign in.\n53. As a Co-VP, I want to reactivate an Account, so that a Position that returns can post again.\n54. As a Co-VP, I want a Deactivated Account's Posts to stay on the site, so that history is not lost.\n55. As a Co-VP, I want the console to refuse to deactivate or demote the last active Admin, so that we cannot lock ourselves out.\n\n### Everyone in the console\n\n56. As an Officer, I want a dashboard with counts of Draft Posts, Published Posts, and Pages, so that I see the state of the site at a glance.\n57. As an Officer, I want one content list of Posts and Pages, newest first, so that I can find anything.\n58. As an Officer, I want to filter that list by Draft/Published and by Post/Page, so that I can find last week's reminder quickly.\n59. As an Officer, I want the list to show each Post's Author as a Position, so that I know which Position wrote it.\n60. As an Officer, I want the same navigation on every console screen, so that I never get lost.\n61. As an Officer on a phone-width window, I want console screens not to scroll sideways, so that they stay usable.\n\n### Running and grading\n\n62. As the developer, I want a seed command that creates the demo Accounts, the three Pages, and a few Posts (at least one Draft, one Published), so that the CMS can be used immediately from a clean clone.\n63. As the developer, I want `cms publish` and `cms deploy` to keep working from the terminal, so that the documented commands still work alongside the button.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Modules\n\n- **Accounts and sessions.** Verifies a sign-in, hashes passwords with argon2, keeps the session in a signed cookie that ends when the browser closes, and exposes one guard for \"must be signed in\" and one for \"must be Admin\". All permission checks go through these guards, never through hidden links alone.\n- **Content.** One module that owns Posts and Pages: saving, status changes, Link generation, deletion, and the rules about who may do what. Routes ask it; they do not decide permissions themselves.\n- **Markdown rendering.** One function turns a Markdown body into sanitized HTML. The editor preview, the local public preview, and the export all call this same function, so nothing can be rendered unsanitized.\n- **Site export.** The existing export function is extended to write the whole public site from Published rows only.\n- **Go live.** Runs the export, pushes the result, and records the time. It is called by the dashboard button and by the `cms deploy` command.\n- **Admin console.** Dashboard, content list, editor, Accounts screen, sign-in screen. Server-rendered templates, no JavaScript framework (ADR-002).\n- **Seed script.** Extended to create demo Accounts, Pages, and Posts.\n\n### Data\n\n- **Account:** sign-in email (unique), display name (the Position, e.g. \"Social Chair\"), password hash, Role (`admin` or `editor`), active flag, created time.\n- **Post:** title, Link (unique among Posts), Markdown body, status (`draft` or `published`), Author (an Account), created time, updated time, first-published time.\n- **Page:** the same fields, plus a marker for which Page is Home.\n- **Site state:** the time of the last Go live, and a count of changes that are Not live yet.\n- Storage is SQLite (ADR-002). The database file is never committed.\n\n### Rules\n\n- **Roles.** Editors: create, edit, publish, unpublish, and delete any Post; edit the body of any existing Page. Admins: everything Editors can do, plus create and delete Pages, change a Page's title and status, manage Accounts, and Go live.\n- **Home.** Created automatically if missing. Cannot be deleted or set to Draft by anyone. Its body holds the standing Study Hall time and place.\n- **Links.** A Post's Link is the date plus a URL-safe form of the title (for example `2026-10-05-study-hall-tonight`). If that Link already exists, a number is added. A Page's Link is the URL-safe form of its title. A Link is set when the item is first Published and never changes after that, even if the title changes or the item goes back to Draft and is Published again. Officers never type a Link.\n- **Dates.** A Post's public date is its first-published time, shown with the weekday. Dates are shown in US Eastern time.\n- **Deleting.** Deleting a Post or Page is permanent and always goes through a confirmation screen. There is no trash.\n- **Accounts.** Accounts are deactivated, never deleted. A Deactivated Account cannot sign in, and an existing session for it stops working. The last active Admin cannot be deactivated or changed to Editor.\n- **Passwords.** Only an Admin sets a password, from the Accounts screen. No password is ever logged or shown.\n- **Not live yet.** Any change that would alter the public site adds one to the count: publishing or unpublishing, editing or deleting something Published. Edits to Drafts do not count. Go live resets the count to zero.\n- **Go live.** Admin only. If the push fails, the console shows a plain error, and the count and last Go live time are left as they were.\n\n### Contracts\n\n- Sign-in is a form posted to `/login` with fields `email` and `password`, matching the template's test helper. The console lives under `/admin`.\n- Every state-changing request is a POST carrying a CSRF token, including sign-out, delete, and Go live. A POST without a valid token is rejected.\n- An anonymous request to any console screen redirects to sign-in. A signed-in Editor requesting an Admin-only screen gets a 403 \"no permission\" screen.\n- Wrong email and wrong password give the same message.\n- `/` on the local app is a preview of the public site and shows Published content only.\n\n### Public site layout\n\n- Home at the site root; one file per other Published Page; one file per Published Post in a posts folder; a Past posts list in that folder; one stylesheet.\n- Navigation: Home first, then the other Published Pages in the order they were created. Past posts is linked from Home, not from the navigation.\n- Home shows its own body, then the latest Published Post in full. Past posts lists the older Published Posts, newest first.\n- Every `href` and `src` is relative. Files in the posts folder reach the stylesheet and the Pages with `../`.\n- No Author is shown publicly.\n- Raw HTML typed into a body is not passed through, and the rendered HTML is sanitized with an allowlist. Images are not in the allowlist.\n\n### Demo data\n\n- The seed creates four Accounts: Co-VP (Admin), and Co-President, Social Chair, and Treasurer (Editors). The Co-VP signs in as `admin@example.test` and the Social Chair as `editor@example.test`, matching the template's test helper; the other two use `copresident@example.test` and `treasurer@example.test`.\n- Passwords come from the environment. All three Editor Accounts use the one Editor demo password.\n- The seed creates Home, About, and Join & Snacks as Published Pages, and at least one Published and one Draft Post.\n\n### Screens\n\n- Every console screen has the same navigation and shows a success or error message after each action.\n- The editor has a formatting hint under the body box (bold, link) and a Preview button that shows the sanitized rendering.\n- Once a Post is live, the editor shows its full public address, built from the configured public site address.\n- No horizontal scrolling at 390 px on the public Home page or the console screens.\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\nA good test here drives the app the way an Officer or Visitor does and checks what they would see: a status code, a redirect, text on a screen, or a file in the exported site. Tests do not reach into the database or call internal functions to check how something was stored.\n\n### Seams\n\nThere are two seams, and both already exist in the template.\n\n1. **The console over HTTP.** Tests use the existing `client` and `client_as(\"admin\" | \"editor\")` fixtures to request screens and post forms. This covers sign-in, Roles, Posts, Pages, the dashboard, the content list, preview, Accounts, CSRF, and Go live.\n2. **The exported site.** Tests call the export into a temporary folder and read the files it wrote. This covers Published-only content, navigation, relative paths, sanitizing, dates, and Links.\n\nOne thing is replaced in tests: the push to GitHub inside Go live. Tests swap it for a fake that records it was called (or fails on purpose), so no test ever pushes to the real repository.\n\nEach test runs against its own temporary database seeded with the demo Accounts, so the fixed test passwords in the fixtures work.\n\n### What gets tested\n\n- Every row of `SECURITY-CHECKLIST.md` has at least one test.\n- Each Role rule has a test for the allowed case and the refused case, requested by direct URL rather than by clicking.\n- Draft content never appears in the export, the local preview, or the Past posts list.\n- A body containing `<script>` and an `onerror=` attribute is harmless in both the preview and the export.\n- Link rules: same-title collision, frozen after Published.\n- Last-Admin protection, Home protection, Deactivated sign-in refusal.\n- Not live yet count goes up on public-affecting changes and resets on Go live; a failed push leaves it unchanged.\n\n### Prior art\n\n`tests/test_t00.py` already uses both seams. It becomes two assertions: anonymous is redirected, and a signed-in Officer sees the dashboard.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Sending the Weekly email. It stays manual; the CMS only supplies the Link.\n- Hosting the snack request form. Join & Snacks links to the Google Form.\n- Scheduled Posts or a calendar.\n- Comments, or any Visitor sign-in.\n- Image uploads, including Officer photos on About, and images linked from other sites. A console upload for Pages with alt text may be added later as a separate `stretch` issue, only after all seven capabilities work.\n- Categories, tags, and search.\n- A trash bin or undo for deleted Posts.\n- \"Forgot my password\" emails.\n- A \"copy last week's reminder\" button. This is the first future improvement.\n- One Account per person (see ADR-003).\n- Putting the console on the internet (see ADR-001).\n- Multi-site, drag-and-drop page builders, and rich-text editors (excluded by the assignment).\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Stage 2 is due Tuesday Oct 6, 2:40 pm, with grace to Wednesday Oct 7, 2:40 pm. Tickets should be ordered so sign-in, Posts, and the export land first.\n- The Monday routine this spec is built around: an Officer writes the Study Hall reminder, marks it Published, a Co-VP presses Go live, and the Officer sends the Weekly email with the Link.\n- \"Publish\" means two different things in everyday speech. In this project, **Published** is a status and **Go live** is the step that reaches Visitors. The `cms publish` command keeps its name because the assignment fixes it; it is the export half of Go live.\n- The Accounts screen is what the assignment calls \"user management\". This covers sign-in, Roles, Posts, Pages, the dashboard, Accounts, and Go live.\n2. **The exported site.** Tests run the export into a temporary folder and read the HTML files it wrote. This covers Published-only content, navigation, relative paths, and sanitizing.\n\nOne piece is faked in tests: the push to GitHub inside Go live, so that no test ever pushes to your real repository.\n\nOne existing test has to change when sign-in is built. It expects anyone to see the \"hello admin\" page without signing in, which contradicts the rule that anonymous visitors are sent to the sign-in screen. I would rewrite it rather than delete it.\n\n## Details I filled in\n\n- **Demo sign-ins:** the seeded Co-VP signs in as `admin@example.test` and the Social Chair as `editor@example.test`, because the template's test helper uses those two addresses. Co-President and Treasurer get `copresident@example.test` and `treasurer@example.test`.\n- **Editors and page titles:** an Editor can edit a Page's body text only. The title (which is the navigation label) and status are Co-VP only.\n- **Navigation order:** Home first, then the other Pages in the order they were created.\n- **Time zone:** post dates are shown in US Eastern time. The brief doesn't say this; it is my assumption.\n- **Public address on the editor screen:** once a Post is live, its editor screen shows the full web address to copy into the Weekly email.\n- **Formatting hint:** a short line under the text box showing how to write bold text and a link.\n- **Images:** not allowed in post or page text at all until the photo stretch ticket.\n\n## Publishing\n\nThe repo has no `spec` or `ready-for-agent` labels yet. The rubric needs `spec` and the skill applies `ready-for-agent`, so I'll create both and put both on the issue.\n\nThe full draft is at `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-msgre-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/8915d99a-a7ca-4e7e-87e5-c294997a06cd/scratchpad/spec.md` if you want to read it first. A ticket with no blockers can start immediately.\n\n**Wide refactors are the exception to vertical slicing.** A **wide refactor** is one mechanical change (rename a column, retype a shared symbol) whose **blast radius** fans across the whole codebase, so a single edit breaks thousands of call sites at once and no vertical slice can land green. Don't force it into a tracer bullet; sequence it as **expand–contract**. First expand: add the new form beside the old so nothing breaks. Then migrate the call sites over in batches sized by blast radius (per package, per directory), each batch its own ticket blocked by the expand, keeping CI green batch to batch because the old form still exists. Finally contract: delete the old form once no caller remains, in a ticket blocked by every migrate batch. When even the batches can't stay green alone, keep the sequence but let them share an integration branch that all block a final integrate-and-verify ticket; green is promised only there.\n\n### 4. Quiz the user\n\nPresent the proposed breakdown as a numbered list.
